# Basenames only, lowercase. Extend this list if a future toolchain script/ledger shows the same
# false-positive pattern -- same "append one entry to grow it" convention as plan-schema-audit's field
# schema.
_NOISE_BASENAMES = {
    "job_queue.py", "job_run.py", "decide.py", "findings_log.py", "idea_log.py", "thought_log.py",
    "skill_manager.py", "lab_env.py", "plan_maintain.py", "plan_sync_check.py", "plan_index.py",
    "plan_liveness.py", "plan_snapshot.py", "plan_schema_audit.py", "plan_files_audit.py",
    "plan_shadow_read.py", "build_edges.py", "session_wrap.py", "session_resume.py",
    "gauge_check.py", "common.py", "claude.md",
    "job_queue.jsonl", "decisions.jsonl", "findings.jsonl", "ideas.jsonl", "thoughts.jsonl",
    "session_events.jsonl", "skill_suggestions.jsonl", "_memory_edges.jsonl", "plan_snapshots.jsonl",
}


def _extract_files(text):
    """basename (lowercase) -> set of as-seen normalized (lowercase, forward-slash) forms, for every
    file-path-shaped token in free text, minus `_NOISE_BASENAMES`. A cheap regex, not a parser --
    good enough for a warning signal a human/agent still judges, not for anything load-bearing."""
    out = defaultdict(set)
    for m in _FILE_TOKEN_RE.findall(text or ""):
        norm = m.replace("\\", "/").lower()
        base = norm.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
        if base in _NOISE_BASENAMES:
            continue
        out[base].add(norm)
    return out


def _pick_repr(forms):
    """Longest as-seen form (more directory context = more specific/informative) -- e.g. prefers
    'core/cat.py' over a bare 'cat.py' seen elsewhere in the same briefing."""
    return max(forms, key=len)


def file_overlaps(tier3_rows):
    """Cheap cross-group file-overlap check -- the always-on half of the F-0891 fix. Extracts file
    tokens from every Tier 3 row's OWN `briefing` text and flags any pair from DIFFERENT groups
    (different `plan` slugs, or either/both ungrouped) that name an overlapping basename. Pairs
    WITHIN one group are not re-flagged here -- job_run's own tier3_groups already serializes those
    (SKILL.md step 8); this exists specifically for the cross-group blind spot the grouping itself
    cannot see. Returns a list of {"kind": "exact_file", "confidence": "high", "jobs": [id, id],
    "plans": [p, p], "files": [...]} dicts, one per colliding pair, `jobs` sorted for determinism."""
    warnings = []
    seen_pairs = set()
    extracted = [(_extract_files(r.get("briefing", "")), r) for r in tier3_rows]
    for i in range(len(extracted)):
        files_a, a = extracted[i]
        if not files_a:
            continue
        group_a = a.get("plan") or f"_ungrouped_{a['id']}"
        for j in range(i + 1, len(extracted)):
            files_b, b = extracted[j]
            if not files_b:
                continue
            group_b = b.get("plan") or f"_ungrouped_{b['id']}"
            if group_a == group_b:
                continue
            overlap_keys = set(files_a) & set(files_b)
            if not overlap_keys:
                continue
            pair = tuple(sorted((a["id"], b["id"])))
            if pair in seen_pairs:
                continue
            seen_pairs.add(pair)
            files_repr = sorted(_pick_repr(files_a[k] | files_b[k]) for k in overlap_keys)
            plans_by_id = {a["id"]: a.get("plan"), b["id"]: b.get("plan")}
            warnings.append({
                "kind": "exact_file", "confidence": "high", "jobs": list(pair),
                "plans": [plans_by_id[pair[0]], plans_by_id[pair[1]]], "files": files_repr,
            })
    warnings.sort(key=lambda w: w["jobs"])
    return warnings


# ── Deeper version: UDMS-coupled files (opt-in, --udms-check) ──────────────────────────────────────
_UDMS_SCRIPT = Path(r"C:\UDMS\udms.py")
_UDMS_STRONG_LAYERS = {"STATE", "CONTRACT"}  # real, ~certain evidence per CLAUDE.md's own framing
_UDMS_WEAK_LAYERS = {"TEMPORAL", "STATIC"}   # probabilistic -- gated on PMI below
_UDMS_PMI_THRESHOLD = 1.0  # bits (~2x lift or better) before a TEMPORAL/STATIC hit counts as "high"

_ENTITY_RE = re.compile(r"entity='([^']*)'")
_LAYER_RE = re.compile(r"evidence_layer='([^']*)'")
_PMI_RE = re.compile(r"pmi_bits=([0-9.eE+-]+)")


def _parse_investigation_queue(items):
    """`udms.py check --json`'s `investigation_queue` is a list of Python dataclass repr STRINGS,
    not nested JSON objects (confirmed directly, 2026-09-06: `check nodes/inner_monologue_node.py
    --json --repo C:\\Nascence`) -- regex-pluck entity/evidence_layer/pmi_bits out of each rather
    than trying to json.loads a repr. A malformed/unexpected entry is skipped, not fatal."""
    out = []
    for s in items or []:
        me = _ENTITY_RE.search(s)
        if not me:
            continue
        ml = _LAYER_RE.search(s)
        mp = _PMI_RE.search(s)
        try:
            pmi = float(mp.group(1)) if mp else 0.0
        except ValueError:
            pmi = 0.0
        out.append({"entity": me.group(1), "layer": ml.group(1) if ml else None, "pmi_bits": pmi})
    return out


def _udms_check_file(path, repo=None, timeout=60):
    """One `udms.py check <path> --json` subprocess call -> list of {entity, layer, pmi_bits} dicts,
    or None on ANY failure (no C:\\UDMS install, non-zero exit, bad JSON, timeout, file not findable
    in the target repo's git history). Never raises -- this is best-effort enrichment; job_run.py
    must keep working with zero UDMS install present. Timed directly against this repo, 2026-09-06:
    ~15-17s per call, cold or not -- no cross-process warm cache observed, unlike the MCP server's own
    session-lifetime topology cache (see CLAUDE.md's UDMS section) -- so callers must cap how many of
    these they issue, not assume a second call is cheap."""
    if not _UDMS_SCRIPT.exists():
        return None
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, str(_UDMS_SCRIPT), "check", path, "--json", "--repo", str(repo or ct.ROOT)],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, cwd=str(_UDMS_SCRIPT.parent),
        )
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            return None
        return _parse_investigation_queue(json.loads(proc.stdout).get("investigation_queue"))
    except Exception:
        return None


def udms_overlap_warnings(tier3_rows, exact_pairs, limit=12, timeout=60):
    """Deeper version of the F-0891 check (opt-in -- see --udms-check on `plan`): for cross-group
    Tier 3 pairs that name NO exact-overlapping file (i.e. not already in `exact_pairs`, the
    {(id,id), ...} set `file_overlaps` produced), ask UDMS whether their named .py files are
    structurally coupled (evidence_layer STATE/CONTRACT -- a real AST/state dependency) or show a
    high-PMI co-change pattern (TEMPORAL/STATIC with pmi_bits >= _UDMS_PMI_THRESHOLD) -- and if so,
    surface the SAME warning shape at confidence "low", mirroring this project's own
    verified/inferred distinction (CLAUDE.md's own "STATE/CONTRACT ... always worth checking" vs
    "TEMPORAL/STATIC ... genuinely uncertain" framing). A DOCUMENTED-layer hit or a low-PMI
    TEMPORAL/STATIC one is NOT surfaced -- per the dossier's own hypothesis text, doc-co-reference
    alone is "not... code coupling" evidence.

    Only queries QUALIFIED .py candidates (has a "/", i.e. some directory context -- a bare filename
    can't be passed to `udms.py check` meaningfully) and only one `udms.py check` call per UNIQUE
    file across the whole batch (memoized), capped at `limit` -- each call is a real ~15-20s
    subprocess (see `_udms_check_file`), so an uncapped run across a large Tier 3 batch could take
    minutes. Returns (warnings, meta) where meta = {"queried": [...], "truncated": bool,
    "unreachable": [...]} so a truncated/degraded run says so instead of silently under-reporting."""
    extracted = {r["id"]: _extract_files(r.get("briefing", "")) for r in tier3_rows}
    plan_of = {r["id"]: r.get("plan") for r in tier3_rows}
    candidates = {}
    for jid, files in extracted.items():
        reprs = {f_repr for base, forms in files.items() for f_repr in [_pick_repr(forms)]}
        candidates[jid] = {f for f in reprs if f.endswith(".py") and "/" in f}

    ids = [r["id"] for r in tier3_rows]
    pairs = []
    for i in range(len(ids)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ids)):
            a, b = ids[i], ids[j]
            group_a = plan_of[a] or f"_ungrouped_{a}"
            group_b = plan_of[b] or f"_ungrouped_{b}"
            if group_a == group_b:
                continue
            pair = tuple(sorted((a, b)))
            if pair in exact_pairs or not candidates[a] or not candidates[b]:
                continue
            pairs.append(pair)

    involved_ids = {jid for pair in pairs for jid in pair}
    unique_files = sorted({f for jid in involved_ids for f in candidates[jid]})
    truncated = len(unique_files) > limit
    to_query = unique_files[:limit]
    dossiers = {f: _udms_check_file(f, timeout=timeout) for f in to_query}
    unreachable = sorted(f for f, d in dossiers.items() if d is None)

    def _lookup(from_file, to_candidates):
        dossier = dossiers.get(from_file)
        if not dossier:
            return None
        for to_file in to_candidates:
            hit = next((e for e in dossier if e["entity"].lower() == to_file.lower()), None)
            if hit:
                return to_file, hit
        return None

    warnings = []
    for pair in pairs:
        a, b = pair
        found = None
        for fa in sorted(candidates[a] & set(to_query)):
            hit = _lookup(fa, candidates[b])
            if hit:
                found = (fa, hit[0], hit[1])
                break
        if not found:
            for fb in sorted(candidates[b] & set(to_query)):
                hit = _lookup(fb, candidates[a])
                if hit:
                    found = (fb, hit[0], hit[1])
                    break
        if not found:
            continue
        f_from, f_to, hit = found
        layer, pmi = hit.get("layer"), hit.get("pmi_bits", 0.0)
        if layer in _UDMS_STRONG_LAYERS:
            reason = f"{layer} layer (structural: real AST/state dependency)"
        elif layer in _UDMS_WEAK_LAYERS and pmi >= _UDMS_PMI_THRESHOLD:
            reason = f"{layer} layer, PMI={pmi:.2f} bits (co-change pattern)"
        else:
            continue
        warnings.append({
            "kind": "udms_coupled", "confidence": "low", "jobs": list(pair),
            "plans": [plan_of[pair[0]], plan_of[pair[1]]], "files": sorted({f_from, f_to}),
            "detail": f"udms.py check {f_from} -> {f_to}: {reason}",
        })
    warnings.sort(key=lambda w: w["jobs"])
    return warnings, {"queried": to_query, "truncated": truncated, "unreachable": unreachable}


# ── Stale in_progress surfacing (F-1389/J-1017, 2026-09-15) ────────────────────────────────────────
# job_run's own tiering above only ever looks at status=="open" jobs. Cross-referencing job_queue.jsonl
# directly showed the status=="in_progress" population is dominated by a legitimate, intentional
# pattern -- restart-gated / multi-day-read / cooldown-gated reads deliberately left open until a
# real-world wait condition clears (e.g. "after Du's next restart", "multi-day (>=5d) post-deployment
# read") -- NOT stale/abandoned work, so this deliberately does not make in_progress dispatchable. It
# only surfaces which in_progress jobs have been open long enough that their own wait condition
# (usually named in plain English in the job's own title) plausibly already cleared -- age alone is the
# signal, same "pure warning for a human/agent's own judgment" spirit as decision_flags/
# file_overlap_warnings above. See F-1389 for the full evidence trail (13 jobs 9-11 days old as of
# 2026-09-15, sitting outside 8 straight batches' visibility).
_STALE_DAYS_DEFAULT = 7.0


def _parse_dt(s):
    """ISO datetime string (job_queue.py's own `NOW.isoformat()` format, tz-aware, e.g.
    '2026-09-04T22:28:49.581711+00:00') -> aware datetime, or None if missing/unparseable. Never
    raises -- a bad/missing `started` value just drops that job from staleness consideration rather
    than crashing the whole `plan` command."""
    if not s:
        return None
    try:
        dt = datetime.fromisoformat(s)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if dt.tzinfo is None:
        dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return dt


def stale_in_progress(in_progress_rows, stale_days=_STALE_DAYS_DEFAULT):
    """For every in_progress row whose own `started` timestamp is more than `stale_days` old, return
    {"id", "title", "started", "plan", "days_open"} (days_open rounded to 1 decimal), sorted
    oldest-first (most likely to be worth a look first). A row with a missing/unparseable `started` is
    skipped, not guessed at. Deliberately does NOT attempt to parse/understand each job's own specific
    wait condition (e.g. "after 1 week" vs "post-restart") -- that is real plan-domain judgment for
    whoever reads this list, not something to fake with a regex; age alone is the signal. Pure
    surfacing -- callers must never treat this list as auto-actionable (see module docstring)."""
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    out = []
    for r in in_progress_rows:
        started_dt = _parse_dt(r.get("started"))
        if started_dt is None:
            continue
        days_open = (now - started_dt).total_seconds() / 86400
        if days_open <= stale_days:
            continue
        out.append({
            "id": r["id"], "title": r["title"], "started": r["started"],
            "plan": r.get("plan"), "days_open": round(days_open, 1),
        })
    out.sort(key=lambda x: x["days_open"], reverse=True)
    return out


def _is_hold(ruling):
    return bool(ruling) and ruling.strip().lower().startswith("hold")


def _decision_flags(plan_slug, spawned_from):
    """Structural decide.py pre-check (J-0262, 2026-08-25 -- built after J-0205 caught D-0035's
    active Hold only via a dispatched agent's own judgment, not any structural check, and two
    job-run batches since papered over the gap with a prompt-level reminder line that won't survive
    a differently-worded future dispatch). Looks up EVERY decision tied to this job -- by matching
    `plan` slug (a plan can have several decisions, and the Hold blocking a job need not be the one
    named in its own `source`) AND by the job's own `spawned_from` decision id if it has one (covers
    a decision whose `plan` field doesn't match the job's, an edge case but cheap to cover) -- and
    reports which are still OPEN (unruled) or RULED-but-Hold (ruling text starts with 'hold', the
    same convention decide.py's own rulings already use, e.g. D-0021/D-0025/D-0029/D-0035/D-0041).
    A job with either non-empty list here must NOT be treated as a plain go-ahead -- see SKILL.md
    step 6."""
    rows = dc.load()
    matches = [r for r in rows if r.get("plan") == plan_slug]
    if spawned_from and spawned_from.get("type") == "decision":
        did = spawned_from["id"]
        if not any(r["id"] == did for r in matches):
            hit = next((r for r in rows if r["id"] == did), None)
            if hit:
                matches.append(hit)
    return {
        "active_holds": sorted({r["id"] for r in matches if _is_hold(r["ruling"])}),
        "open_decisions": sorted({r["id"] for r in matches if r["ruling"] is None}),
    }


def _slim(r):
    flags = _decision_flags(r.get("plan"), r.get("spawned_from"))
    return {
        "id": r["id"], "title": r["title"], "plan": r.get("plan"), "urgency": r["urgency"],
        "category": r["category"], "source": r.get("source"),
        "lab_mode": r["lab_mode"], "isolation": r.get("isolation", "none"),
        "decision_flags": flags,
    }


def tier_of(r):
    if r["category"] == "backfill":
        return 1
    if r["category"] == "doc" or (r.get("source") or "").startswith(_TIER2_SOURCE_PREFIXES):
        return 2
    return 3


def compute(rows, udms_check=False, udms_check_limit=12, stale_days=_STALE_DAYS_DEFAULT):
    ready_open = [r for r in rows if r["status"] == "open" and r["autonomy"] == "ready"]
    tiers = {1: [], 2: [], 3: []}
    for r in ready_open:
        tiers[tier_of(r)].append(r)
    for t in tiers.values():
        t.sort(key=lambda r: (-r["urgency"], r["created"]))

    file_overlap_warnings = file_overlaps(tiers[3])
    udms_meta = None
    if udms_check:
        exact_pairs = {tuple(w["jobs"]) for w in file_overlap_warnings}
        udms_warnings, udms_meta = udms_overlap_warnings(tiers[3], exact_pairs, limit=udms_check_limit)
        file_overlap_warnings = file_overlap_warnings + udms_warnings

    tier3_groups = defaultdict(list)
    for r in tiers[3]:
        key = r.get("plan") or f"_ungrouped_{r['id']}"
        tier3_groups[key].append(_slim(r))

    blocked = [r for r in rows if r["status"] == "open" and r["autonomy"] == "needs_input"]
    in_progress = [r for r in rows if r["status"] == "in_progress"]

    out = {
        "tier1": [_slim(r) for r in tiers[1]],
        "tier2": [_slim(r) for r in tiers[2]],
        "tier3_groups": dict(tier3_groups),
        "file_overlap_warnings": file_overlap_warnings,
        "needs_input_count": len(blocked),
        "in_progress": [_slim(r) for r in in_progress],
        "stale_in_progress": stale_in_progress(in_progress, stale_days=stale_days),
    }
    if udms_meta is not None:
        out["udms_check_meta"] = udms_meta
    return out


def _apply_limit(items, n):
    return items if n is None else items[:n]


def _apply_group_limit(groups, n):
    if n is None:
        return groups
    flat = sorted((r for g in groups.values() for r in g), key=lambda r: -r["urgency"])[:n]
    keep_ids = {r["id"] for r in flat}
    out = defaultdict(list)
    for key, items in groups.items():
        kept = [r for r in items if r["id"] in keep_ids]
        if kept:
            out[key] = kept
    return dict(out)


def cmd_plan(a):
    plan = compute(jq.load(), udms_check=a.udms_check, udms_check_limit=a.udms_check_limit,
                   stale_days=a.stale_days)
    plan["tier1"] = _apply_limit(plan["tier1"], a.tier1_limit)
    plan["tier2"] = _apply_limit(plan["tier2"], a.tier2_limit)
    plan["tier3_groups"] = _apply_group_limit(plan["tier3_groups"], a.tier3_limit)
    # A job trimmed out of this batch by --tier3-limit shouldn't still show up in a warning -- the
    # warning is about two jobs that would actually be DISPATCHED together, not two jobs that merely
    # exist in the backlog.
    kept_ids = {r["id"] for g in plan["tier3_groups"].values() for r in g}
    plan["file_overlap_warnings"] = [w for w in plan["file_overlap_warnings"]
                                      if all(jid in kept_ids for jid in w["jobs"])]

    if a.json:
        print(json.dumps(plan, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
        return

    n3 = sum(len(v) for v in plan["tier3_groups"].values())
    n_warn = len(plan["file_overlap_warnings"])
    n_stale = len(plan["stale_in_progress"])
    print(f"# job-run plan — tier1 (backfill): {len(plan['tier1'])} · tier2 (hygiene): "
          f"{len(plan['tier2'])} · tier3 (real work): {n3} across {len(plan['tier3_groups'])} plan-groups"
          + (f" · {n_warn} FILE-OVERLAP WARNING(S)" if n_warn else ""))
    print(f"# {plan['needs_input_count']} open jobs waiting on founder input (not in this run — see "
          f"`job_queue.py list --needs-input` / /decide-review) · {len(plan['in_progress'])} already "
          f"in_progress (check these aren't stale before starting a new run)"
          + (f" · {n_stale} look STALE (> {a.stale_days:g}d — see below)" if n_stale else ""))

    if plan["stale_in_progress"]:
        print(f"\n## STALE-LOOKING IN-PROGRESS ({n_stale}) — in_progress > {a.stale_days:g} day(s) old "
              f"(F-1389/J-1017). Most in_progress jobs are a legitimate, intentional pattern "
              f"(restart-gated / multi-day-read / cooldown-gated, deliberately left open until a "
              f"real-world wait condition clears) — this is NOT saying these are stale/abandoned, only "
              f"that they've been open long enough their own condition MAY already be satisfied. Age "
              f"alone is the signal; still your own judgment call to open each one and check its actual "
              f"wait condition (often named in its own title) before acting — never auto-act on this "
              f"list.")
        for r in plan["stale_in_progress"]:
            print(f"  {r['id']} [{r['plan'] or '—'}] {r['days_open']:.1f}d open (started {r['started']}) "
                  f"{r['title'][:70]}")

    print()
    print("## Tier 1 — backfill (mechanical, dispatch freely in parallel)")
    for r in plan["tier1"]:
        print(f"  {r['id']} [{r['plan']}] {r['title'][:70]}")
    print("\n## Tier 2 — hygiene fixes (small, bounded, dispatch freely in parallel)")
    for r in plan["tier2"]:
        flags = " ISOL" if r["isolation"] == "required" else ""
        print(f"  {r['id']}{flags} {r['title'][:70]}  (source: {r['source']})")

    if plan["file_overlap_warnings"]:
        print(f"\n## FILE-OVERLAP WARNINGS ({n_warn}) — cross-plan-group jobs naming the same file "
              f"(F-0891/J-0635). job_run's own tier3_groups only serializes jobs sharing a `plan` "
              f"slug; these pairs sit in DIFFERENT groups and would otherwise dispatch in full "
              f"parallel with no signal either way. A PURE WARNING, not auto-serialized — SKILL.md "
              f"step 8's 'never let two Tier 3 agents touch the same plan doc' generalizes to 'same "
              f"file, any plan'; whether to actually serialize this pair is still the dispatching "
              f"session's own judgment call.")
        for w in plan["file_overlap_warnings"]:
            tag = "EXACT" if w["kind"] == "exact_file" else "UDMS"
            detail = f" — {w['detail']}" if w.get("detail") else ""
            print(f"  ⚠ [{w['confidence']}/{tag}] {' + '.join(w['jobs'])} "
                  f"(plans: {', '.join(str(p) for p in w['plans'])}) share {', '.join(w['files'])}{detail}")
        meta = plan.get("udms_check_meta")
        if meta:
            note = f", {len(meta['unreachable'])} unreachable" if meta["unreachable"] else ""
            trunc = " — TRUNCATED, raise --udms-check-limit for full coverage" if meta["truncated"] else ""
            print(f"  # --udms-check queried {len(meta['queried'])} file(s){note}{trunc}")
        elif not a.udms_check:
            print("  # (--udms-check not passed — this run only checked EXACT file-name matches, "
                  "not UDMS structural/co-change coupling between differently-named files)")

    print("\n## Tier 3 — real work, grouped by plan (serialize within a group, parallelize across groups)")
    print("# Before ruling on ANY decision, check this job's own `decision_flags` (or run "
          "`decide.py show D-XXXX` directly) -- an ACTIVE_HOLD is a founder ruling still in force, "
          "not a courtesy reminder to re-derive; do not override it without new founder input.")
    warn_by_job = defaultdict(set)
    for w in plan["file_overlap_warnings"]:
        a_id, b_id = w["jobs"]
        warn_by_job[a_id].add(b_id)
        warn_by_job[b_id].add(a_id)
    for plan_slug, items in sorted(plan["tier3_groups"].items(), key=lambda kv: -max(r["urgency"] for r in kv[1])):
        flags = "  [SEQUENTIAL — multiple jobs on this plan]" if len(items) > 1 else ""
        print(f"  ── {plan_slug}{flags}")
        for r in items:
            f2 = []
            if r["isolation"] == "required":
                f2.append("ISOL")
            if r["lab_mode"]:
                f2.append("LAB")
            df = r.get("decision_flags") or {}
            if df.get("active_holds"):
                f2.append(f"ACTIVE_HOLD:{','.join(df['active_holds'])}")
            if df.get("open_decisions"):
                f2.append(f"OPEN_DECISION:{','.join(df['open_decisions'])}")
            if r["id"] in warn_by_job:
                f2.append(f"FILE_OVERLAP:{','.join(sorted(warn_by_job[r['id']]))}")
            fs = f" [{'/'.join(f2)}]" if f2 else ""
            print(f"     {r['id']}{fs} {r['title'][:70]}")


def cmd_show_tier(a):
    plan = compute(jq.load())
    if a.tier == 1:
        rows = plan["tier1"]
    elif a.tier == 2:
        rows = plan["tier2"]
    else:
        rows = [r for g in plan["tier3_groups"].values() for r in g]
    print(json.dumps(rows, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="job_run")
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    lp = sub.add_parser("plan")
    lp.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    lp.add_argument("--tier1-limit", type=int, default=None, dest="tier1_limit")
    lp.add_argument("--tier2-limit", type=int, default=None, dest="tier2_limit")
    lp.add_argument("--tier3-limit", type=int, default=None, dest="tier3_limit")
    lp.add_argument("--udms-check", action="store_true", dest="udms_check",
                     help="Opt-in deeper file-overlap check (F-0891/J-0635): for cross-group Tier 3 "
                          "pairs with no exact file-name match, shell out to C:\\UDMS\\udms.py check "
                          "per named .py file (~15-20s per unique file, no cross-process warm cache) "
                          "and flag a STATE/CONTRACT structural hit or high-PMI co-change pair at "
                          "confidence 'low'. Off by default -- can add minutes to `plan` on a big "
                          "batch; see --udms-check-limit to bound it.")
    lp.add_argument("--udms-check-limit", type=int, default=12, dest="udms_check_limit",
                     help="Max unique files run through `udms.py check` when --udms-check is set "
                          "(default 12). Each call is a real ~15-20s subprocess -- this is a hard "
                          "cap on wall-clock cost, not a quality knob.")
    lp.add_argument("--stale-days", type=float, default=_STALE_DAYS_DEFAULT, dest="stale_days",
                     help="F-1389/J-1017: an in_progress job whose own `started` timestamp is more "
                          "than this many days old is surfaced in the 'STALE-LOOKING IN-PROGRESS' "
                          "report section (default 7). Pure surfacing, never auto-dispatched -- most "
                          "of the in_progress population is intentionally long-lived (restart-gated / "
                          "multi-day-read / cooldown-gated), so this is a signal for a human/agent to "
                          "judge, not a verdict.")
    lp.set_defaults(fn=cmd_plan)

    ls = sub.add_parser("show-tier")
    ls.add_argument("tier", type=int, choices=[1, 2, 3])
    ls.set_defaults(fn=cmd_show_tier)

    a = p.parse_args()
    a.fn(a)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
=== END FULL FILE CONTENT ===

title: Find why the substrate tick stalls during sleep (63 growing study-watchdog hits, F-1421)
briefing:
Source: F-1421 (J-1025's own read, docs/findings.jsonl), plan actions_expansion
(docs/staged/actions_expansion.md). Read F-1421 in full first -- this briefing summarizes it, F-1421
carries the full citations.

WHAT'S ALREADY ESTABLISHED (verified, not to be re-derived): every study-bound
"[locomotion] WATCHDOG completed a stuck journey" line in data/nascence.log (78 total, whole log
history) splits into two mechanisms. 15 are ordinary restart recovery (a journey in-flight when the
process last stopped, cleaned up by the first tick after the next boot) -- fully benign, exactly
core/locomotion.py's own documented design, NOT this job's concern. The other 63 (100% to study, zero
exceptions, two independently-cross-validated ways) are a real, live, worsening bug: core/night.py's
to_bed() (line 110) begins a real multi-leg locomotion journey to study as the first action of EVERY
sleep cycle (nodes/inner_monologue_node.py's _enter_sleep(), line 777), and that journey then sits
completely un-ticked -- core/orchestrator.py's _substrate_loop (an independent asyncio Task that should
call locomotion.tick() every ~5s unconditionally, no asleep-gate anywhere) simply does not get scheduled
-- for the WHOLE span until the sleep pipeline's own chapter-formation/journal/world-pass/downscale/
dream stages finish. That span has grown in lockstep with two independent measures (the watchdog's own
"started Ns ago" value AND data/night_log.jsonl's own recorded per-night duration_s), from ~900-950s in
late August to 1500s+ by 09-12/13, and in daily frequency from 0-2/day before 09-06 to 7-9/day
(matching or exceeding that day's total sleep-cycle count) from 09-06 onward. It also leaves
sensorium.state["location"] reporting Du's PRE-sleep place, not "study", for that whole span while
state["asleep"]=True is already set (code-verified: core/sensorium.py's move()/begin_journey() path
only flips location once locomotion.tick() processes a leg) -- a real state-consistency gap, not just a
cosmetic delay.

WHAT F-1421 DID NOT ESTABLISH (this job's real work): the exact line/mechanism that prevents
_substrate_loop's asyncio Task from being scheduled during the sleep pipeline. F-1421 already ruled out
the single most likely cause -- core/model_client.py's LLM client is genuinely async (aiohttp
throughout; grepped clean of requests./subprocess./run_in_executor/time.sleep(). Trace forward from
there, live and/or by further static reading: core/chapters.py's try_form_chapter(), core/journal.py's
write_entry(), whatever core/night.py's stage 5 "world pass" (consolidation sweep + observe-only shadow
passes) and stage 8 DREAM actually call, and core/memory/store.py's own synchronous sqlite3 usage under
a large/growing row count (replay_strengthen, downscale_episodic, day_material's queries) -- sqlite3 in
Python is inherently synchronous per-call, and if any of these queries has gotten slow as the store has
grown (matching F-1421's own noted-but-not-chased hypothesis that the SAME growth is what's slowing the
whole pipeline), a long synchronous DB call on the event-loop thread would explain exactly this
starvation without needing any blocking HTTP call at all. Confirm or rule this out with real
measurement (e.g. time individual stages/queries directly, or instrument _substrate_loop's own tick
cadence during a live sleep cycle next time Du is running) rather than assuming.

WHAT TO DO ONCE THE MECHANISM IS FOUND: propose a fix. Plausible candidate shapes (not a ranked
recommendation -- evaluate on evidence): (a) whatever synchronous work is found gets moved off the
event-loop thread (e.g. run_in_executor) or made to yield periodically; (b) core/night.py's own
pipeline calls locomotion.tick() explicitly between stages so a sleep-onset journey always completes on
schedule regardless of the outer scheduler's behavior; (c) to_bed() stops using a real multi-leg
journey for the sleep transition specifically and flips state["location"] to "study" instantly instead
(closes the state-inconsistency gap directly, sidesteps the watchdog dependency entirely for this one
case, but changes the departure-narration UX slightly -- he currently perceives the walking-there line
as he falls asleep); (d) leave the watchdog path as the mechanism but shorten _WATCHDOG_S specifically
for the sleep case so the location-inconsistency window is bounded tighter. If, once the real mechanism
is understood, the right fix turns out to be a genuine founder-taste call (this plan's own D-0209/D-0224
precedent is the shape to match), open a /decide rather than picking one unilaterally -- but don't
open one speculatively before the mechanism itself is actually known.

ALSO WORTH FIXING ALONGSIDE (low-effort, not the main point): nodes/inner_monologue_node.py:798's own
code comment ("the full ~20-25 min pipeline") is stale -- night_log.jsonl's real duration_s for
09-09..09-12 is routinely 45-90 minutes now.

Update docs/staged/actions_expansion.md's Current State (stack newest-first, do not rewrite F-1421's own
entry) with whatever this job finds, per this project's usual convention.

title: Fresh core/+nodes/ json.load( grep for the remaining ~41-50% unattributed event-loop residual (F-1422 spawn)
briefing:
Context (self-contained -- read F-1238, F-1328, F-1403, F-1422 in full via findings_log.py show for
the complete numeric trail before starting; also read docs/staged/data_store_hygiene.md's Current
State stack, especially the F-1422/J-1029 and F-1403/J-0959 sections):

F-1238 (J-0847) found the post-D-0154-flip climate tick still runs ~1.27 s/tick over its 5 s nominal
schedule. F-1328 (J-0885) isolated-timed ClimateEngine.tick() at 157.7 ms median -- only ~12.4% of
that overrun -- and named event-loop starvation by OTHER coroutines' synchronous blocking file I/O
as the likely driver, pointing at 4 specific heavy-subconscious-file readers found via a repo-wide
grep of `json.load(` across core/+nodes/ (17 hits total that session; only these 4 were individually
characterised at the time). J-0959 (F-1403) directly timed the first (subconscious_node._save_state,
~0.51-0.61 s/tick depending on cadence statistic). J-1029 (F-1422, this job's own parent finding)
directly timed the other 3 (curiosity_node._select_seeds, dream_node._load_top_tensions,
tension_ledger's two functions, combined ~0.050 s/tick). COMBINED, all 5 named candidates now
account for 0.560-0.660 s/tick depending on mean-vs-median cadence basis -- 50.3%-59.3% of F-1328's
own 1.1123 s/tick climate-unattributed residual. This straddles D-0216's own "most of the residual"
defeater bar without clearly clearing it (same genuinely-mixed character J-0959 already found for
its own single candidate) -- meaning a real, substantial ~0.45-0.55 s/tick (41-50%) gap is STILL
unattributed even crediting all 5 named candidates their full measured share.

D-0216 itself (`python decide.py show D-0216`) carries an active founder HOLD as of 2026-09-14 --
check its CURRENT status before doing anything with it; if still held, do not rule it regardless of
what this job finds (only the founder lifts a Hold); this job's task is investigation, not a ruling.

The task: F-1328's own `json.load(` grep across core/+nodes/ found 17 hits total that session, of
which only the 4 now-timed candidates (+ subconscious_node's own read-before-write, folded into
J-0959's already-timed _save_state) were individually characterised. Re-run that grep fresh
(`grep -rn "json\.load(" core/ nodes/` or equivalent -- also check `json.loads(` separately, a
distinct call some modules may use for an already-read string) against the CURRENT tree (files may
have changed since 2026-09-14; re-verify hit count, don't assume it's still 17) and characterise
EVERY hit this session and F-1328's own session did NOT already name: which heavy file does it read
(is it data/subconscious_state.json again, or a DIFFERENT heavy file -- data/frontier.json,
data/pursuits_active.json, data/geometry_tuples.jsonl, or something not yet on anyone's radar?),
what calls it and how often (mirror J-0959's/J-1029's own method: a structured sidecar log if the
module already writes one, else a text-log marker, else a direct DB query if the caller-side gate
writes to a queryable table -- do not guess a cadence from code-reading alone, this project's own
house rule), and whether it runs synchronously on the SAME asyncio event loop climate's tick shares
(a call already offloaded to a thread/executor, like core/coupling_rides.py's own daemon-thread
_collect_ledgers() that F-1328 already noted as a GIL-contention outlier candidate rather than a
steady-median one, is a DIFFERENT kind of candidate -- note it as such, don't lump it in as if it
were another synchronous-blocking source).

For any new hit that turns out to be a real, non-trivial, non-rare synchronous blocking reader (by
the same duty-cycle test: cost_median_s / cadence_s_mean x 5s nominal tick, matching F-1403/F-1422's
own method exactly, cite them for the formula), direct-time it the same way (lab_env.isolate(),
db="copy" only if it touches the DB, N=50 unless impractically slow -- justify a smaller N if so)
and add its own contribution to the running total. Record ONE finding (or split by candidate if
warranted, matching F-1422's own precedent for when to split) with real numbers, --confidence
verified only where both cost AND cadence are independently measured. Update docs/staged/
data_store_hygiene.md's Current State (append at the bottom of the existing stack, right before
"Earlier state -- verified 2026-09-05", keep every existing section's text intact). Do NOT rule
D-0216 regardless of what this job finds -- state plainly in the finding and the plan-doc update
whether the running total NOW plausibly covers "most" of the 1.1123 s/tick residual, so whoever next
reviews D-0216 (founder ruling, or /decide-review) has the complete, final picture across every
named `json.load(` hit, not just the original 4+1.

If the fresh grep finds NOTHING new and material (e.g., the remaining hits are all genuinely
rare/gated, or already offloaded off the event loop, or read tiny files), that is itself a valid,
useful finding -- it would mean the ~41-50% residual gap's source is NOT among the already-grepped
`json.load(` call sites at all, and the event-loop-lag probe D-0216 itself asks about (observe real
event-loop stalls directly, joined against nascence.log's other coroutine activity in the same
window) may be the only way left to find it -- say so plainly if that is where this job lands; that
would be new, real evidence bearing on D-0216's own GO option, still not a ruling this job makes
itself.

title: Re-read isolate_outcomes.jsonl once a genuine 5-7+ day window has actually elapsed (J-1031: only ~5h of the required ~120-168h had passed)
briefing:
From finding:F-1423 (J-1031). J-1031 re-read data/_lab/_isolate_outcomes.jsonl on 2026-09-15T13:38 local: 18 rows now (5 deleted/27.8%, 13 locked/72.2%, up from J-1013's 16), but elapsed time since the log's own creation (2026-09-15T08:27:14 local) was still only ~5h11m -- about 3-4% of the required 5-7+ day (120-168h) window. worked example). Re-derive every line number fresh rather than trusting this briefing's -- other
jobs may land on core/orchestrator.py first and shift them. The 6 locations found as of this
briefing (2026-09-15):

1. Lines 165-167 -- module-level comment directly above the PROC_* constants block, only 11-13
   lines above the retirement comment in the SAME block: "...a MASTERED match (proficiency >=
   AUTOMATIC) also bypasses the deliberative reconstruction nodes (Recall + Episodic Buffer) --
   automaticity."

   per-cycle dispatch method: "...and (when mastered) streamline the pipeline."

   handles this kind of moment without laborious reconstruction -- skip Recall (and, downstream,
   the buffer)."

   streamlines the pipeline (see _procedure_automatic)."
6. Lines 2433-2437 -- _procedure_automatic()'s own docstring: "True when a recognised procedure is
   mastered enough to run autonomously -- i.e. to bypass the deliberative reconstruction nodes
   (Recall + Episodic Buffer)." (The method body itself is correct, live code -- only its

   whether proficiency ever reaches the retired, unreachable PROC_AUTOMATIC_PROFICIENCY
   threshold -- see its own 2026-08-22 retirement comment." rather than describing a reachable

title: Fix two confirmed literal_will/hands regex gaps: retrospective-blocker adjacency, determiner-guard killing bare "cup/pot of tea" wants
briefing:
F-1442 (study_upgrade, following up F-1301) found two separate, confirmed-by-direct-execution regex bugs
in the shared want-grammar (core/hands.py wants() + core/literal_will.py) while tracing why the
2026-09-05 "tea I just made" monologue thought produced no ledger row. Both were confirmed by importing
the REAL functions from C:\Nascence and calling them directly (not re-implemented) -- see F-1442's
evidence for the exact scripts/output. Neither needs a founder ruling (D-0226 covers the separate design
question of whether monologue generation needs a narrative grounding check at all); these are two
mechanical regex fixes to existing, already-intended guards.

BUG 1 -- retrospective blocker adjacency gap (core/literal_will.py, _B_RETRO, ~line 78-80):
`_B_RETRO = re.compile(r"\b(yesterday|last night|earlier i|this morning i)\b|\bi (lit|laid|stoked|fed|
gathered|collected|fetched|brewed|watered|sowed|planted|wrote|kept|combed|made|went|walked|tended)\b")`
requires "i" immediately adjacent to the verb (exactly one space). Confirmed by direct regex execution:
matches "i made" but NOT "i just made" (or presumably "i already made", "i finally made", etc -- any
adverb insertion). This blocker exists specifically to stop retrospective/already-done phrasing from
being read as a live want (core/hands.py's wants()/_blocked() docstring: "literal_will's BLOCKERS
(negation, wish, hypothetical, retrospective, ...)"), so this gap defeats its own purpose for a very
ordinary class of real phrasing. Suggested fix: allow 0-2 intervening words between "i" and the verb,
matching the tolerance already used elsewhere in this same grammar (see the _NOT_NOUN-adjacent "a verb
is a verb" fix history below for the project's own precedent of hardening a boundary regex). e.g.
`\bi(?:\s+\w+){0,2}\s+(lit|laid|...)\b` -- but check this does not start over-blocking genuine present
wants that happen to contain "i" + 1-2 words + one of these verb-forms in a non-retrospective sense
(rare, since these are specifically past-tense verb forms, not infinitives -- "i want to make" does not
match "made", so should be low-risk; add regression cases for both).

BUG 2 -- _NOT_NOUN determiner-guard kills bare noun-phrase want-triggers (core/literal_will.py, _NOT_NOUN,
line 199; applied inside core/hands.py wants()'s main matching loop, line 132). _NOT_NOUN =
`(?<!the )(?<!a )(?<!an )(?<!that )(?<!this )(?<!its )(?<!my )(?<!his )(?<!her )(?<!their )`, added
2026-09-04 (git a36f37b / 8214013, "J-0554... a verb is a verb") to stop a determiner-preceded word being
misread as a verb ("the pull of that rusted trap" is not a weeding will). Confirmed by direct execution
this ALSO silently defeats the tea latch's own bare noun-phrase trigger entries "cup of tea" / "pot of
tea" (nodes/inner_monologue_node.py ~line 3373-3379) whenever they are preceded by a/the/my etc -- which
is nearly always how they occur in real English:
  wants(text, tea_verbs) results (tea_verbs = the exact tuple at inner_monologue_node.py:3373-3379):
    "I would love a cup of tea right now." -> False
    "I want a cup of tea." -> False
    "I could really use a pot of tea." -> False
    "I want tea." -> False (separate, narrower gap: no trigger is the bare word "tea" alone)
    "I want to make a pot of tea." -> True   (works: "make" is not determiner-preceded)
    "I want to brew a pot of tea." -> True   (works, same reason)
This means a real, present-tense, unambiguous want for tea phrased WITHOUT an explicit make/brew/boil/
steep/put-the-kettle verb in front of "cup of tea"/"pot of tea" currently never dispatches -- likely a
real, silent loss of genuine tea deeds, not just a guard against false ones. Suggested fix: either (a)
exempt whole-noun-phrase trigger entries (ones with no verb at their head, like "cup of tea"/"pot of
tea"/"a hot drink") from the _NOT_NOUN prefix in wants()'s matching loop -- they were never meant to be
read as a verb in the first place, so the noun-vs-verb disambiguation _NOT_NOUN exists for does not apply
to them; or (b) add "cup of" / "pot of" as their own short trigger fragment that isn't determiner-gated.
Check whether ANY other latch elsewhere in nodes/inner_monologue_node.py uses a similar bare noun-phrase
trigger (grep for verbs tuples with an entry containing no verb, e.g. "of" without a preceding verb word)
-- this may not be tea-specific.

Both bugs live in core/literal_will.py, a small, heavily-shared, high-fan-in module (this exact file has
had J-0554/F-0761, J-0787/F-1128, J-0799/F-1149, J-0800 as recent hardening passes on this same
boundary-regex machinery per its own git log) -- per this repo's CLAUDE.md, run
`udms_get_change_dossier` on core/literal_will.py (and core/hands.py) before editing, and add real
regression tests (both a positive case that now passes and a negative case confirming the blocker/guard
still fires where it should) rather than hand-verifying only the two cases above. Do NOT hand-edit any
.jsonl store; this is a pure source-code fix. Record a findings-log entry citing the before/after
wants()/_blocked() output for both bugs once fixed.

  A3 dormant only (re-feed kept): isolates the dormant effect from the re-feed effect.
Fixed 3 scenes in every arm (MAX_EPISODES forced to 3 for the experiment) so length is not a variable.

title: Add explicit sensorium.tick() calls between night.py sleep-pipeline stages (F-1469 fix)
briefing:
Source: F-1469 (J-1042), plan actions_expansion. Read F-1469 in full first for the real evidence (it
carries full citations; this briefing summarizes).

WHAT'S ESTABLISHED: F-1421 measured that during every sleep-onset journey (core/night.py's to_bed(),
called as literally the first action of every sleep from nodes/inner_monologue_node.py's _enter_sleep(),
line ~777), core/orchestrator.py's _substrate_loop asyncio Task -- which should call locomotion.tick()
every ~5s unconditionally -- gets ZERO real scheduling opportunity for the whole sleep-pipeline span
(900-1500s in late August, now routinely 2800-5400s), so the sleep-onset journey (legs are 20-90s) sits
un-ticked until core/locomotion.py's own 900s watchdog force-completes it. This has grown in lockstep
with the memory store's size and is now the NORMAL path (7-9/day) rather than a rare edge case, and it
leaves sensorium.state["location"] reporting Du's PRE-sleep place for the whole span while
state["asleep"]=True is already set -- a real state-consistency gap.

F-1469 confirmed the process runs ONE persistent asyncio event loop for its whole life (ruling out a
separate-loop bug) and found real, measured, non-yielding synchronous call sites inside the pipeline
(core/memory/store.py's _embed() -- a plain synchronous SentenceTransformer.encode() call fired on every
fragment write -- and replay_strengthen()'s per-group queries, which SQLite's planner services via the
least-selective index, idx_layer, scanning close to the full 87,645-row episodic set rather than the
wake-block window: measured 0.776s for one group query alone against the live 713MB DB). These are real
and architecture-consistent but not proven to be the complete explanation for the full span (live
tick-cadence instrumentation during an actual sleep cycle was not attempted).

THE FIX (recommended by F-1469, NOT a founder-taste call -- no perceived UX changes): have
core/night.py's own stage sequence call `from core import sensorium as _s; _s.tick()` explicitly between
stages of the sleep pipeline (right after to_bed(), and again after each subsequent stage -- chapter
formation, journal, world-pass, downscale, DREAM, etc., wherever _enter_sleep in
nodes/inner_monologue_node.py currently calls `_night.stage(...)`). This works regardless of the exact
root cause of the asyncio starvation, because it is a direct synchronous call from within night.py's
already-synchronous stage-sequencing code -- not reliant on the background Task ever getting a
scheduler turn. sensorium.tick() already self-rate-limits to one real tick per 5 real seconds (module-
level _last_tick guard, core/sensorium.py line ~3298-3300), so calling it defensively between slow
stages is safe and cheap -- it either does real work or returns instantly.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Read F-1469 and F-1421 in full first (docs/findings.jsonl).
2. Add explicit `sensorium.tick()` calls at each stage boundary inside nodes/inner_monologue_node.py's
   _enter_sleep() (or centralize it inside core/night.py's own stage() helper if that reads cleaner --
   founder taste on WHERE, not WHETHER, to add it -- use judgement).
3. Verify locally: this should NOT be tested by writing to the live running Du process's own data store
   (Du may be live -- check with `netstat -ano | findstr 1143` first) or by touching the shared
   C:\Nascence tree destructively. Use a throwaway worktree of HEAD (per this project's own CLAUDE.md
   git-safety rule) or a scratch script constructing a minimal asyncio harness that exercises
   _enter_sleep-shaped stage sequencing with a synthetic slow synchronous stage, to confirm
   sensorium.tick() actually advances a pending journey leg when called mid-pipeline.
4. Record a finding on whether the fix actually closes the state-inconsistency window (does
   sensorium.state["location"] now flip to "study" promptly instead of sitting stale for the whole
   pipeline?).
5. Update docs/staged/actions_expansion.md's Current State with the result, and commit.
6. This does NOT require reverting/skipping the real multi-leg journey (option (c) in F-1421/J-1042's
   own briefings) and does NOT need a founder /decide -- it changes no perceived UX (Du still perceives
   the walking-there line exactly as today), only internal tick scheduling. If in the course of this
   work you find the fix does NOT fully close the gap (i.e. something else independent of tick
   scheduling is also involved), that is new evidence worth its own finding, not a reason to force the
   job closed.

title: Harden job-run's Tier 2 commit-step guidance against same-file multi-agent collision (F-1549)
briefing:
F-1549 (verified, filed by J-1132) found that job-run's own Tier 2 ground-rules text tells each dispatched agent to commit its edit with a plain "git add <path> && git commit", but when two Tier 2 agents edit non-overlapping regions of the SAME shared file (observed: docs/ROADMAP.md, three different jobs J-1126/J-1131/J-1132 all editing it in one batch), whichever agent commits first sweeps up every other agent's still-uncommitted, unrelated hunk in that file into its own commit with no mention in the commit message. No data was lost this time, but attribution is wrong, and a second agent that pre-staged its own change from a since-superseded HEAD (normal if it fetched HEAD before the first agent committed) could easily produce a destructive commit that silently reverts the first agent's now-landed work -- the same failure shape CLAUDE.md already documents for git stash/reset, produced here by ordinary git add+commit instead.

What to do: update job-run's (and nurse-rounds', which dispatches the same Tier 2 population) own ground-rules template for the commit step. At minimum, add an explicit instruction to re-check the file against a FRESH `git log`/`git diff` (or re-run `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` and compare against whatever base the agent's own edit was made against) immediately before committing a shared file that other Tier-2 jobs might also be touching, so a stale pre-staged commit is never fired blind. Better: document (or adopt as the new default recipe) the non-destructive, worktree-free method J-1132 actually used and verified working this session -- stage only your own hunk via `git show HEAD:<path>` + apply your own edit to that copy + `git hash-object -w` + `git update-index --cacheinfo 100644,<blob>,<path>` (index-only, never touches the working tree, never requires git reset/stash/checkout) -- as a safer alternative to a blind `git add <path>` when a job cannot be sure it is the only agent that touched that file this batch. This is a real gap in the existing ground-rules text, not something J-1132 should fix unilaterally mid-job (it's the shared dispatch template read by every Tier 2 agent, not a Nascence code/plan file) -- hence spawned as its own job rather than edited in place.

title: garden.harvest(): an unnamed harvest ask should skip herbs in regrow cooldown instead of pinning to pool[0] (F-1628)
briefing:

title: Break the 25-minute sleep-onset event-loop freeze: make core/chapters.py find_cluster()'s O(n^2) seed loop non-blocking and behaviour-identical (F-1648)
briefing:
SOURCE: F-1648 (root cause, inferred; read it in full first), F-1647 (J-1085's read: J-1075's sensorium.tick() fix did NOT reduce the sleep-onset watchdog rate) and F-1649 (a one-phrase correction to F-1648: read 'no line' where it says 'exactly one line'). Plan: actions_expansion (F-1421 / F-1469 / F-1483 are the chain this closes).

WHAT IS KNOWN. Every full sleep freezes Du's whole asyncio event loop for about 1,480 s (24.6 min), starting immediately after the '[monologue] sleep replay' log line and ending at find_cluster's own '[chapters] cluster of N found ...' log line (nascence.log 09-19 01:44:17.154 -> 02:08:48.715; 09-21 09:41:11.274 -> 10:05:51.820). The cause is core/chapters.py find_cluster() -- a plain def called directly from try_form_chapter() before its first await -- whose seed selection (lines 141-144: for every candidate vector v, count the vectors w with np.dot(v, w) >= CLUSTER_SIM 0.70) is all-pairs. The candidate set (level 0: origin in subconscious_synthesis / inner_thought / active_imagination, chapter_id NULL, embedding not null, older than 48 h) is n = 33,589 today, so 1.13e9 np.dot calls; a microbenchmark of the identical expression predicts ~1,220 s vs ~1,480 s observed, and it grows with n^2 (this is F-1421's monotonic growth and its 09-06 step change: the freeze crossed the 900 s locomotion watchdog). During the freeze nothing on the loop runs: no substrate tick, no stability tick, no log line. Consequences: the sleep-onset journey is completed by the 900 s watchdog instead of ticking through its 20-90 s legs (7-9 per day), sensorium.state['location'] is stale at the pre-sleep place for ~25 min of every sleep-with-journey, the process is unresponsive ~3-4 h a day, and ~25 of every 55-80 sleep minutes are this one function. J-1075's four explicit _night.tick() calls (nodes/inner_monologue_node.py:935, 950, 973, 1216 at HEAD) fire as designed but only after this function returns, so they change nothing on their own.

THE JOB. Make find_cluster stop blocking the loop while selecting EXACTLY the same seed and cluster as today. Recommended (both parts, they are independent): (1) compute the neighbour counts in blocks with one float32 matrix product per block (V[i:j] @ V.T >= CLUSTER_SIM, summed over axis 1; 512-1024 rows per block; ~433 GFLOP in total at n=33.6k, i.e. seconds rather than 20+ minutes on this machine's BLAS) and keep the 'first maximum wins' rule (strict > when updating best_n) so the same seed is chosen; (2) call find_cluster via asyncio.to_thread (or await asyncio.sleep(0) between blocks) from try_form_chapter so the loop keeps ticking even when the work takes seconds. If the founder wants sleep length unchanged, ship ONLY part (2): it stops the freeze and the watchdog, and leaves the algorithm and the sleep length as they are. Leave _era_window, _cooled, MIN_MEMBERS, CLUSTER_SIM and everything after the seed loop untouched. core/chapters.py has one caller (nodes/inner_monologue_node.py:927) and has not changed since the 2026-08-27 baseline commit.

(b) Speed: time the new path at full size on the copy (expected: seconds); do NOT run the old loop at full size (20+ minutes of a core). title: Fix the declined-redirect teleport: make begin_journey()'s J-1040/J-1111 declines a true no-op through sensorium.move(), log each decline, and test through move() (F-1653)
briefing:
SOURCE: F-1653 (the defect; verified, read it in full first), F-1654 (the rate read's status and the re-derived baseline), F-1468 (J-1040, the same-destination gate), F-1525 (J-1111, the first-leg gate), D-0224 (ruled by Travis 2026-09-18: protect only a journey's first leg), F-1418. Plan: actions_expansion. This is a REGRESSION that is live in Du's running process (since the 2026-09-18 23:14 restart), so it is not a taste question and should be fixed at the next restart.

WHAT IS KNOWN. core/locomotion.py begin_journey() returns None for four different reasons: LOCOMOTION off, an empty path (already there), a same-destination retrigger (J-1040) and a first-leg cross-destination redirect (J-1111). Its only caller, core/sensorium.py move() (lines ~2579-2592), reads every None as 'LOCOMOTION off' and falls through to the rollback 'state["location"] = target; _save_now()' plus the instant arrival narration. For the two new decline cases that is a teleport to the requested place while d["journey"] stays pending in data/position.json, and locomotion.tick() then flips his location to the next place on the OLD path (a garden->shore journey shows garden -> shore (instant) -> wood -> shore). Live evidence (F-1653): 0 of 597 'DISPATCH move' narrations were instant-move text before the restart, 27 of 47 since; 25 of the 34 same-cycle route_act+dispatch pairs; in 11 of the 27 the trace location later moves to another place with no new decision, 10 of them through the wood. A second-order effect: get_position() takes its place from the sensorium's location, so after a teleport p['place'] no longer equals journey['departure'] and the first-leg gate does not fire for the NEXT redirect. Neither J-1040's nor J-1111's harness went through sensorium.move(); the comment in begin_journey() ('every existing caller's fallback path already handles this correctly') was never tested.

THE FIX. Make a declined redirect a TRUE NO-OP: the ruling (D-0224) and J-1040's intent are that the in-progress journey is left completely untouched and nothing moves him. title: Part 1 of F-1648: fast block-matrix find_cluster, each sleep about 20-25 min shorter; Travis to decide the rhythm change (J-1180 shipped part 2; F-1659, F-1648)
briefing:
THE QUESTION FOR TRAVIS. After J-1180 (merged to master as f10500f) the roughly 25-minute chapter-formation scan no longer freezes Du, but it still costs about 1,480 s (24.6 min) of every full sleep and grows with the square of the store (n = 33,589 today; the last 14 sleeps' freeze was 1,439-1,626 s). PART 1 replaces the all-pairs Python loop with blocked float32 matrix products (seconds instead of about 25 min). It is the same answer, but it makes each full sleep about 20-25 minutes shorter (8-10 sleeps a day, so roughly 3-4 fewer hours a day in the sleep state; night_log duration_s from about 3,600-4,900 s to about 2,400-3,600 s; 'you slept about N minutes' 64-81 down to about 40-55). Do you want that rhythm change? Options: (A) ship it; (B) ship it only when the scan crosses a size you name (n grows; 1,440 s becomes about 2,000 s at n about 39k); (C) do not ship: the loop is free now, and the scan is harmless except for its growth. Rule it with a defeater (via /decide). Nothing to build until this is ruled.

ORIGINAL PART-1 TEXT (from J-1177/J-1180, unchanged): "(1) compute the neighbour counts in blocks with one float32 matrix product per block (V[i:j] @ V.T >= CLUSTER_SIM, summed over axis 1; 512-1024 rows per block; about 433 GFLOP in total at n=33.6k, i.e. seconds rather than 20+ minutes on this machine's BLAS) and keep the 'first maximum wins' rule (strict > when updating best_n) so the same seed is chosen. Leave _era_window, _cooled, MIN_MEMBERS, CLUSTER_SIM and everything after the seed loop untouched."
FOUNDER-VISIBLE SIDE EFFECT (from J-1177, adjusted): each sleep becomes about 20-25 min shorter. (The 'location flips within about a minute of lying down' half is ALREADY delivered by J-1180.) Check that nothing in core/sleep_pressure.py, core/night.py or the waking text ('you slept about N minutes') assumes the current 45-90 min length, and update the comment at nodes/inner_monologue_node.py near line 910 (J-1042 wrote 'routinely 45-90 minutes now'), which becomes stale.

IF APPROVED - BUILD PLAN. Start from J-1180's harness: scripts/_test_find_cluster_off_loop.py already holds a FROZEN verbatim copy of the base-commit find_cluster, synthetic datasets D1-D6 (clusters plus decoys, exact ties, 300 threshold pairs, levels 1 and 2, boundaries, a read-only sample of 2,400 real rows), a heartbeat, a write-audit hook and section [7]'s GIL-releasing-callback recipe. Its section [1] (AST proof) is PART-2-only: replace it.
1. Exactness by construction, not by luck: float32 SGEMM and per-pair sdot can differ in the last bits, so a pair within about 1e-5 of 0.70 may flip. Compute G = V[i:j] @ V.T, then take every entry with |G - CLUSTER_SIM| < 1e-4 and RE-DECIDE it with the exact per-pair _cosine (expected about 1e4-1e5 pairs at n=33.6k: about 0.1 s). Decisions then equal the old loop's exactly, the count vector is identical, the seed (np.argmax = first maximum) and the membership are identical.
2. Equivalence test: (a) the COUNT VECTOR, row for row (not just the seed), old loop versus new, on real-row subsamples of n = 2,000-4,000 taken as several disjoint read-only LIMIT/OFFSET windows (the old loop takes seconds there), plus D2 (ties) and D3 (300 pairs within +-3e-7) plus a denser 5,000-pair band within +-1e-5; report every differing row and whether the seed or membership changed (expect 0); (b) full-size speed on synthetic 33.6k x 384 unit vectors, no DB (expect seconds); NEVER run the old loop at full size (25 min of a core); (c) the heartbeat again on the new path; (d) the in-flight guard and cancellation tests from J-1180's section [5].
3. Loop behaviour: with the scan down to seconds of large BLAS calls (which release the GIL for milliseconds), a thread may now be fine where it was not for the per-pair loop: measure with section [7]'s recipe before choosing thread versus a yield per row block. OpenBLAS can use up to 24 threads: a few-second burst on the 64-thread 3970X, where the CPU-hosted local models also run, so check the contention.
4. F-1662's residual: with the scan in seconds, the 0.3-1 s candidate fetch plus vector build becomes the dominant blocking stretch: consider fetchmany chunks with a yield, in the same change.
5. Restart-gated. Read job after at least 3 full sleeps on the new merge commit: duration_s should fall by about 1,400-1,600 s per sleep, '[chapters] cluster of N found' N (and CHAPTER FORMED) must keep appearing and agree with the old loop's answers on the same store (recompute one on a read-only sample), longest inter-line gap at most 210 s. Du is live: no restart, no live-store write, isolate for anything that touches the DB.

title: FOUNDER CALL: should graduation to 'the same one' count distinct encounters (N = 6 h reusing EVENT_GAP_S, or a few minutes) instead of raw looks? D-0166 item 4 option (ii), deliberately not built by J-1174 (F-1680); Claude recommends leaving it until J-1192's read shows a burst graduation
briefing:
FOUNDER CALL (surfaced by J-1174's build, F-1680; nothing here is built or blocked, this is a design question only you can rule). READ FIRST: F-1680 (the executed numbers), F-1679 (the flock/swarm bar that shipped), F-1622 (the original graduation finding), D-0166 (the ruling item 4 whose option (ii) this is).

THE QUESTION. Graduation to 'the same one' (core/life_traces.py note_sighting, GRADUATE_SIGHTINGS 5 within GRADUATE_WINDOW_S 30 days) counts RAW rendered sightings: every look that shows a creature adds one, however close in time. D-0166 item 4 was built as the flock/swarm/plural bar (26 of the 58 population rows can no longer graduate; the oystercatcher keeps its graduation). D-0166's other candidate, option (ii), was deliberately NOT built: count a sighting toward graduation only when it is at least N minutes after the last counted one, i.e. count distinct ENCOUNTERS rather than looks. Should it be built, and with what N?

THE DATA (F-1680, read-only over the 84 rendered sightings in data\life_events.jsonl up to 2026-09-21 18:30): the 73 consecutive same-row-same-place gaps form a continuum from 6 seconds to days with no natural break (7 under 1 min, 16 under 5, 29 under 15, 33 under 30, 39 under 60, 48 under 120, 53 under 360; median oystercatcher gap 17.9 min). Every gap under 15 minutes belongs to three rows: the oystercatcher (27 of 29), the honeybees (1: the 4th and 5th sightings 6.4 s apart; now closed, honeybees are barred), the korora (1: 72 s apart, one visit). After the flock/swarm bar the live rows an encounter rule would still change are few: for an N of a few minutes only the korora (3 counted sightings, two of them one visit; 2 more raw looks would graduate it), for an N above 73 minutes also the blackbird (3 counted, first two 72.9 min apart). What N does to the oystercatcher's already-graduated history (56 raw sightings): 5th distinct encounter, i.e. its graduation, at 09-11 06:03:30 (raw, and N=5 min), 09-11 07:29:39 (N=30 min), 09-11 16:59:57 (N=2 h), 09-12 02:57:44 (N=6 h, about 21 hours later than raw); by its last sighting it would have 42, 28, 20 and 12 distinct encounters against 56 raw.

OPTIONS. (A) Build nothing: keep raw counting for the 32 rows that can graduate; the demonstrated burst (honeybees) is closed by the bar. (B) Build encounter grain with N = 6 h, reusing life.EVENT_GAP_S (the engine's own 'one arrival/departure event per row and place per six hours'), computed at READ time from the stored recent_sightings list so legacy lists are judged the same way; five distinct presence epochs in 30 days is what 'the hedgehog that visits the saucer nightly' would take: five nights. It delays every eligible row's graduation (the oystercatcher's by about 21 hours on the real data). (C) A shorter N (5-30 min) that only collapses same-visit bursts (korora-style) and leaves the rest alone.

RECOMMENDATION (Claude's, not a ruling): (A) for now. The bar removed the only demonstrated burst; 'what counts as one encounter' is a design question, not a threshold to fit, and J-1192 (the post-restart read of the whole living-world package) will show whether any eligible row actually graduates on a burst of near-simultaneous looks. Revisit (B) or (C) if it does, or if the korora or another eligible row graduates from looks seconds apart.

If you rule (B) or (C): /decide open then /decide rule with a defeater, and a build job is spawned from the ruling; nothing is edited before that.

title: Pick the empty-larder mechanism for the cat (F-1703): A/B/C, C recommended
briefing:

Separately and already known (J-1154, open, not this job's to fix): even a successful note would still need the collect-box leg, which has never once worked for any good in this world's history (0 deliveries collected, ever).

THREE CANDIDATE MECHANISMS (full detail, code sites, and each one's own honest counter-case are in F-1703 -- read it before choosing, this is a summary only):

Weakest case: the will itself may simply be too rare (once ever) for any window width to reliably catch the next occurrence, and it does nothing for the separate, already-broken collection leg.

title: Approve building the two-part sweep()/_cites_this_book fix (word-boundary match + most-specific-subject-first ordering) before further chapter_id clear batches, or leave D-0245's hold as-is (J-1197, F-1704: 2 real collisions found beyond About You, defeater lift-condition (a) not met)

THE PROPOSED FIX (not built; J-1197 was read-only by design). TWO changes, because the two failure modes are different mechanisms:
(1) In `core/world_consolidation.py` `sweep()`: process subjects most-specific-signature-first, so a strictly more specific subject (e.g. "About You Second Edition") claims its own tagged fragments before a shorter, subsuming subject ("About You") can. Fixes the genuine-subset case.

THE QUESTION. RECORD the ruling via `/decide open` then `/decide rule --by travis`, quoting the option chosen; if (A) or (B), a build job follows from the ruling (worktree, UDMS dossier, tests, no live DB write, restart-gated where it changes Du's own read behaviour... actually this affects only offline repair tooling, not Du's live process, so restart-gating may not apply — the build job should check and say). title: core/light.py field_at(): the night moon term ignores wood's own 0.3x canopy scaling (F-1725 spot-check)
briefing:

night-time moon-illumination term to read heavens.moon(now) instead of a real-wall-clock-only
geometry_census.peek() call, restoring scripts/life_smoke.py to 180/0 for the garden place in
December (the only place/month the smoke script itself checks).

THE GAP THIS FOUND. While spot-checking the J-1212 fix beyond life_smoke.py's own December/garden-only
coverage (per that job's own instruction not to overfit the fix to one case), the SAME check
(day(13:00) > dusk(20:00) >= night(23:00), weather clear) FAILS for place="wood" in December:
day=0.300 dusk=0.026 night=0.042. Read core/light.py field_at() (~line 104-187): for place=="wood",
the SKY term is deliberately dimmed by a tree-canopy factor (`v = sky * 0.3`, line ~129, "wood: v =
sky * 0.3") -- but the MOON term added later in the same function (`v += 0.12 *
float(_hv.moon(now)["illum"])`, the J-1212 fix, same place condition `place in ("garden", "shore",
"wood")`) is NOT scaled by that same 0.3x factor: it is a flat addition regardless of place. So at
dusk, wood's residual sky glow is correctly dimmed to 30% of the open-air value, but at night, wood
gets the SAME full moonlight contribution as open garden/shore -- physically backwards (a forest
canopy should block moonlight reaching the ground at night too, not just sunlight at dusk), and it is
what causes the dusk<night inversion for wood specifically.

rule, or a fresh job-run worktree) with:

test-isolation convention -- see scripts/life_smoke.py's own header for the pattern, or J-1212's own

ALSO WORTH A GLANCE, same finding, much smaller and possibly not worth fixing (report either way,

day>dusk>=night inversion for garden itself in July-October, at the SAME hardcoded smoke hours
(20:00/23:00) IF they were checked there too (life_smoke.py itself only checks December). Unlike the
wood gap above, this one is NOT obviously a code bug: in those months real sunset is 17.0-17.8h, so
BOTH 20:00 and 23:00 already fall inside true night (well past the dusk window), and the tiny
inversion is just the moon's own continuous phase drift across those 3 real hours, not a wrong-value
read. Read core/light.py field_at()'s sky-glow computation (the sine-based `sky = cloud *
max(0.0, sin(pi*f))` term for the "sun still up" branch, vs the flat `cloud*0.12` twilight-glow
constant for the "sun down but within daylight()'s dawn/dusk window" branch) and world_clock.py's
_SUN table + daylight()'s +-0.7h dusk/dawn window: near a tabulated sunset, the sine formula troughs
toward 0 right as f->1, then the code jumps to a flat 0.12 constant once the sun is formally "down" --
a real discontinuity in the twilight model that is the more likely root structural cause of BOTH this
residual and (arguably) part of why December's dusk was as low as 0.088 in the first place. Worth
reading and reporting a recommendation (smooth the transition? leave it, since the practical magnitude
is negligible and nothing currently tests it?) rather than fixing blind -- this borders on "what should
'dusk' mean" being a design call, not just a coding bug, per J-1212's own briefing language for the
analogous summer case.

title: Audit 3 other geometry_census.peek()-for-moon_illum call sites for the same now-threading gap J-1212 fixed (F-1725)
briefing:
READ FIRST: F-1725 (verified) and F-1711 (verified). J-1212 found and fixed a bug in core/light.py
field_at(): it read moon illumination via `geometry_census.peek().get("moon_illum")`, which
internally calls `heavens.moon()` with NO time argument (always real wall-clock time), silently
ignoring the simulated `now` field_at() itself was explicitly given -- breaking field_at()'s own
documented "pure function of now" contract (see core/light.py's _sun(now) call, J-0510's rule) and
causing scripts/life_smoke.py's deterministic December light check to fail non-reproducibly (the
failure's exact numbers drifted with real wall-clock time even though the check's own timestamps are
fixed). The fix: call `heavens.moon(now)["illum"]` directly instead of routing through
geometry_census.peek().

THE PATTERN THIS FOUND. Grepping for the same idiom (`grep -rn "geometry_census.peek\|_gc.peek\|GC.peek"
core/*.py nodes/*.py`) turned up FOUR call sites total, not one:
  - core/light.py:172 (field_at()) -- FIXED by J-1212.
  - core/sensorium.py:1100 -- `_sk = _sky.look_up("garden", weather, (_gc.peek() or {}).get("moon_illum"))`
  - core/sensorium.py:1546 -- the same pattern for "shore".
  - core/study_life.py:2023 -- `mi = (_gc.peek() or {}).get("moon_illum")`, same idiom.
None of these three remaining sites were audited by J-1212 (out of that job's own scope). They MAY be
entirely fine as-is: core.sky.look_up() (the function all three ultimately feed) takes its OWN `t`
parameter for star/Cross positions (world_clock.sun(t), heavens.star(key, t)) separately from the
`moon_illum` its caller pre-computes, so if sensorium.py's and study_life.py's own callers never pass
a simulated timestamp through (i.e. they are real-time-only, live-rendering contexts, always
describing the sky "right now"), then a real-time-only moon_illum is CORRECT there and there is no
bug -- unlike field_at(), which explicitly accepts and is used with a simulated `now` (by
scripts/life_smoke.py and other deterministic tests).

TASK. Read core/sensorium.py's two call sites (around line 1100 and 1546) and core/study_life.py's
(around line 2023) in full, including their own enclosing functions' signatures and every caller of
THOSE functions, to determine: does execution ever reach these three geometry_census.peek() calls with
a caller-supplied/simulated timestamp in play (e.g. from a test, a replay tool, or any code path that
threads a `now`/`t` other than "right now") the way life_smoke.py did for field_at()? If yes for any
of the three, that is the same class of bug F-1725 found -- fix it the same way (call
`heavens.moon(<the real now/t in scope>)["illum"]` directly instead of geometry_census.peek(), or
thread a `now` parameter through if the enclosing function does not already have one and genuinely
needs to for a real caller -- do not add a `now` parameter nobody would ever pass just for
symmetry). If no (all three are genuinely real-time-only, never invoked against a simulated
timestamp anywhere in the codebase or its tests), report that plainly as the finding -- "confirmed no
bug, real-time-only contexts" is a complete, valid outcome here, not a failure to dig further. Either
way, record a findings-log entry citing what you actually read/ran, at the confidence the evidence
supports.

Also worth checking while there (same underlying question): does ANY of the three removed-detour
paths' incidental trigger of soundscape.active_sounds()/life.sound_gate() (the side effect F-1725's

title: garden death-cause classifier: give bird predation its own cause (stop mislabelling it neglect)
briefing:
F-1763 (verified, 2026-09-23): core/garden.py's _advance_plant() death-cause classifier (the block right after the `vigour<=0` death check, roughly lines 724-737) has branches for disease/rot/age/pests(aphid-style)/frost_burn only -- no branch for bird predation -- so any plant whose entire vigour-loss traces to the "eaten_by_birds" mechanic (advance(), ~line 475-477, which drains vigour directly and never touches p["pests"]/disease/rot/frost_burn) falls through to the catch-all `cause = "neglect"`. Confirmed against live data: of the 28 real non-weed crop volunteers from the 2026-09-02 germination burst (data/garden.json, read-only), 19 have cause="neglect" despite every one of the 28 having real eaten_by_birds history rows (7-22 bites each for the 19); "neglect" reads as Du's own fault (dried out, unwatered) in the death-line vocabulary (`_DEATH_LINES["neglect"] = "dried to a crisp, brown stalks"`), which is actively MISLEADING for a bird-driven death and would corrupt any future investigate-hand binding he forms about why a plant died (garden_upgrade.md's own §1 law says causes must be discoverable and honest, never a wrong one baked in structurally).

This is a pure bookkeeping/attribution fix, NOT a balance change -- it does not touch how OFTEN or how HARD birds bite, only what gets RECORDED as the cause once a bird-driven death happens. It does not need the founder ruling D-0261 is waiting on (that's about harshness/whether the mechanic itself is too strong, a separate question).

Suggested fix (a minimal, additive change, verify in isolation the same way J-1169 did): add a `bird_bites` counter to the plant dict (or check the plant's own `history` for a recent run of "eaten_by_birds" events with no other stressor active) and give _advance_plant()'s cause classifier one more branch, e.g. `elif bird_bites > 0 and disease<=0.5 and rot<=0.4 and not _aged and pests<=0.5 and frost_burn<=0.6: cause = "birds"` (ordering matters -- keep it as a narrower check than the existing ones, not a blanket override, since a plant can legitimately die from MULTIPLE compounding causes and the existing priority order -- disease > rot > age > pests > frost > neglect -- should probably still take precedence when those other signals are ALSO present; birds slots in as a new, more specific catch before the neglect fallback). title: Living World: choose garden/wood/shore trace wording for cicada, kingfisher, welcome_swallows (no-trace-there vs new phrase) — F-1801
briefing:
