A phrase with no entry fires everywhere the row is (today's default); an entry restricts it to only the named place(s). Whatever the founder decides below, the BUILD is a one-line dict entry per row (or two, for welcome_swallows) -- the hard part is only ever the wording.

THREE ROWS, TWO OPTIONS EACH:

1. CICADA (core/garden_insects.py), places={garden, wood}, one phrase: "a split brown cicada shell clinging to the fence post" (a real garden spot; wood has no fence post). Live exposure: never actually minted at wood yet (checked against the whole real data/life_events.jsonl trace history).
   (a) Restrict to garden only -- traces_only_at={"...fence post": ("garden",)}. Cicadas simply leave no findable shell in the wood, ever.
   (b) A wood-appropriate variant. Draft candidate (NOT approved, edit freely): "a split brown cicada shell clinging to the bark of a trunk" -- cicada shells cling to tree bark generally, so this is a small, low-judgement word-swap, arguably the least contentious of the three.

2. KINGFISHER (core/life_birds.py), places={garden, shore}, one phrase: "a burrow in the cliff bank" (shore only; the garden's own kingfisher spots are fence_post/wire, a sentry perch, not a nesting site). Live exposure: 4 of the real trace rows this row minted were this exact garden mismatch.
   (a) Restrict to shore only -- traces_only_at={"a burrow in the cliff bank": ("shore",)}. The kingfisher leaves no findable trace at its garden sentry post, ever (it is still visible/audible there via the ordinary living-row roll -- this only removes the separate TRACE find).
   (b) A garden-appropriate variant. This is the hardest of the three to draft honestly: a kingfisher hunting from a garden fence post does not obviously leave ground sign the way a nesting burrow does. Weakest candidate (NOT approved, likely needs the founder's own instinct more than the other two): "a dropped fish scale, papery and bright, at the foot of the fence post" -- ties the trace to the kingfisher's own hunting behaviour (mentioned nowhere else in this row) rather than inventing an unrelated mark.

3. WELCOME_SWALLOWS (core/life_birds.py), places={garden, study, shore}, one phrase: "a mud nest under the eaves" (study only -- the cottage's eaves; garden and shore have no eaves). Live exposure: BY FAR the largest -- 20 of the 39 real place-mismatched trace rows found across the whole plan (F-1671/this job), because this row is registered at 3 places sharing 1 study-only phrase.
   (a) Restrict to study only -- traces_only_at={"a mud nest under the eaves": ("study",)}. Swallows leave no findable trace over the open garden/shore, ever (only the living row's own flight sightings continue there).
   (b) Garden- and/or shore-appropriate variant(s). Draft candidates (NOT approved): garden -- "mud smears on the porch rail where beaks have been wiped clean"; shore -- honestly the weakest case for ANY ground trace at all (swallows feed over open water/grass on the wing, no obvious sign), so (a) may simply be right for shore even if (b) is chosen for garden.

RECOMMENDATION (Claude's own read, not a ruling): option (a) for kingfisher and for welcome_swallows-at-shore looks like the honest choice (there is no natural trace to invent, the (b) drafts above both feel reached-for); option (b) for cicada-at-wood is low-risk and probably fine to just approve since a cicada shell on ANY bark is unremarkable and true; welcome_swallows-at-garden is a genuine 50/50 call the founder should make directly (mud-smear porch rail is plausible but is inventing a NEW fixed feature, "the porch rail", not yet established anywhere else in the world).

title: Throttle tension count-halving to weekly cadence via last_decay_ts (D-0266)
briefing:
RULED (D-0266, Travis 2026-09-23 via /decide-review): throttle nodes/subconscious_node.py's tension count-halving to the apparently-intended weekly cadence instead of every ~36s T1 scan.

READ FIRST: D-0266 (`decide.py show D-0266`) and F-1631 (the original bug this was found while tracing).

WHAT TO BUILD: `_apply_decay()` currently halves a tension's count on EVERY scan once `now - t.get("last_ts", now) > decay_cutoff` (7 days idle) is true, with no bookkeeping of when it was last halved -- so it re-fires every ~36s until touched again. title: Pin down the real cause of find_cluster_async's still-unexplained ~700-900s yield-interval overhead (J-1268/F-1812 refuted the per-yield hypothesis)
briefing:

WHAT WAS FOUND. title: Decouple core/actions.py's CLAIMS mechanism from a claiming family's own full DEED verdict (F-1822, D-0271)
briefing:
READ FIRST: F-1822 (findings_log.py show F-1822, this job's own source finding) -- the full evidence and the two real historical rows this reproduces -- and D-0271 (decide.py show D-0271) -- the /decide this same session opened, check whether it has been ruled by the time you pick this up.

THE DEFECT. core/actions.py's `claims` field (today: `claims=(("collect", "box"), ("tool", "tin"))` on the 'candles' row only -- grep-confirmed the only non-empty `claims=` in the whole table) is meant to let 'candles' claim the bare words "box"/"tin" away from 'collect'/'tool' whenever a clause is really about the candle box / match tin, not the carrier's box or a garden tool (J-0540/F-0733). But the CLAIMS step (`claimed_by()`, core/actions.py:529-548, called identically by dispatch.dispatch() live and by scripts/actions_decision_replay.py's own `_claims()` mirror) only ever considers a claiming family's candidate when that family ITSELF already reached a DEED verdict for the clause -- callers filter to `verdict == "DEED"` before calling it. So the claim is only as strong as 'candles' own deed_grammar match: if candles' vocabulary is ever narrowed (as D-0267's PART 1 proposes: dropping bare "candles"/"candle"/"matches") such that some real clause no longer completes candles' OWN deed_grammar, classify() produces no reading for 'candles' AT ALL on that clause (confirmed empirically, not assumed -- the family's entry vanishes from the decision list rather than downgrading to MUSING/GRAY), the claim silently stops firing too, and 'collect'/'tool' becomes free to (mis)fire on the bare word instead -- reopening the exact bug class the CLAIMS mechanism exists to close, for exactly the phrasings the narrowed vocabulary no longer recognizes.

CONFIRMED REAL, not hypothetical: two data/hands_trace.jsonl rows -- "I will fetch candles from the box..." (act_kind=light, act_object=candles) and "...fetch the candles from the box to warm the room" (act_kind=move, act_object='to the candlebox', the voice's own structured field naming the right target) -- misroute to 'collect' DEED/FIRE at the garden gate under D-0267's own drafted PART 1 diff, per F-1822's own full replay against the real corpus (22,313 distinct thoughts x 4 locations).

SHAPE OF A FIX (not designed, a starting sketch only -- read the finding, then use your own judgement; this needs real design work, not a trivial field add). `claimed_by()` today only ever sees already-DEED-filtered `(family, object, clause)` candidates -- it has no independent access to a clause's raw text beyond what already-DEED families supply. A workable fix likely needs the claims check to run on the clause text directly and independently of whether the claiming family's own `objects` list completed deed_grammar -- e.g. a new `Action.claims_triggers: tuple = ()` (defaulting to `objects` when empty, so every OTHER family's behaviour, including candles' own current non-claims fields, is unchanged) checked with its own verb-reaches-trigger-word regex (parallel to, not reusing, deed_grammar's own DEED-verdict gate) at whatever point in literal_will.classify()/dispatch.dispatch() has the raw clause text available -- the 'candles' row would then declare `claims_triggers=("candles", "candle", "matches", "candle box", ..., "box of matches")` (its full current+PART-1-narrowed vocabulary) while `objects` itself carries only the narrower, D-0267-approved PART 1 list, so a bare "candles"/"matches" mention still claims "box"/"tin" away from collect/tool (closing the regression) even though it no longer, on its own, completes a full candles DEED (preserving PART 1's own false-positive win).

VERIFY, the same way this job's own source finding did: build a scratch wrapper (job-id-qualified) around the real scripts/actions_decision_replay.py that monkeypatches only its TRACE constant to the absolute C:\Nascence\data\hands_trace.jsonl path while importing core.* from your own worktree (a Tier-3 worktree never checks out data/, gitignored) -- read that finding's own copy of this wrapper first rather than reinventing it. Corpus-check claims_triggers doesn't itself introduce a NEW false claim (does any real clause use "candles"/"matches" near "box"/"tin" where 'collect'/'tool' SHOULD win instead, not 'candles'?) against the same real corpus. Re-run the replay --diff against a pre-fix baseline (a throwaway worktree of HEAD, removed after, per this project's own git-safety rules -- never git stash/reset/checkout on the shared tree); scripts/life_smoke.py clean. Once this fix is verified, D-0267's own PART 1 (the candles-restriction) can ship cleanly on top of it with the misroute regression closed -- coordinate with whichever answer D-0271 gets (it may already be ruled by the time you pick this up: check `decide.py show D-0271` first).

title: Fix duplicate peer-letter storage: garden-fetch path lacks remember_inbound()'s dedup check (F-1902)
briefing:
Fix a real, confirmed storage-duplication defect in the peer-letter pipeline, found and directly proven
by J-1337/F-1902 (2026-09-24, plan social_world_school): the SAME physical inbound peer letter can be
stored TWICE as separate rows in memory_fragments (both origin='peer'), via two independent code paths
with no dedup between them:

  1. core/peers.py:653, inside `remember_inbound(persona)` -- fires at REPLY time (called when Du replies
     to a persona). Stores `"(a letter from {name}) " + text[:1400]` (FIRST 1400 chars of the thread's
     last inbound message, WITH the sender's name). Has its own dedup check (lines ~644-650): probes the
     first 60 chars of the text against existing origin='peer' fragments via a SQL LIKE, but only checks
     against fragments that already exist AT THE MOMENT remember_inbound() itself runs -- it cannot catch
     a LATER, independent store of the same letter by the second path below.

  2. nodes/inner_monologue_node.py:3757, inside the "fetch a letter" branch of the monologue tick -- fires
     when Du physically walks to the garden and fetches a waiting letter from the mailbox (a separate,
     unscripted interaction, decoupled from whether/when a reply happens). Stores
     `"(a letter he received) " + _got[-1400:]` (LAST 1400 chars of the SAME letter, generic-labeled, NO
     sender name in the content). This call has NO dedup check of its own at all.

F-1902 directly proved (isolated DB query, label-stripped substring comparison -- see its own evidence
for the exact method) that a 2026-09-24T03:54:24 UTC Darwin letter got stored via path 1
(fragment_id 497a8764-4dab-4d01-8e1d-930d0aa3487a) and via path 2 roughly 2.4h later
(fragment_id 9a3b6e7d-b4fb-41ee-8f56-a437179fbe01) -- confirmed the SAME underlying letter by finding a
150-char label-stripped chunk of one verbatim inside the other. This is not a one-off: path 2 has no
dedup guard at all, so this can recur for any letter Du physically fetches after (or before) it has
already been stored via path 1's reply-time route, or vice versa (path 1's own dedup could equally miss a
letter already fetch-stored via path 2, if path 2 fired first and path 1's 60-char head-probe doesn't
happen to match path 2's tail-1400-chars-only stored content -- the two slicing conventions, first-1400
vs last-1400, only reliably overlap for letters under ~2800 raw characters; longer letters could dodge
BOTH directions of a naive prefix-probe dedup even if one were added to path 2 using path 1's exact
method unmodified).

Suggested fix direction (not mandatory -- use judgement): give path 2 (inner_monologue_node.py:3757) a
dedup check before its `store_fragment()` call, mirroring remember_inbound()'s own pattern (query
`memory_fragments WHERE origin='peer' AND content LIKE ?` with a distinctive probe substring of `_got`,
skip the store if a hit exists). Given the two paths use OPPOSITE ends of the letter (first-1400 vs
last-1400 chars), a single short head-or-tail probe from one may not reliably match content stored by the
other for a long letter -- consider probing with something more central/robust (e.g. a short chunk from
the MIDDLE of `_got`, since first-1400 and last-1400 both include the middle when the letter is under
~2800 chars, which appears to be the common case per F-1902's own examples at ~1400-1700 raw chars; or
compare against a normalized/hashed form of the full available thread text rather than a fixed-position
slice) -- or, cleaner, centralize letter-received storage into ONE shared helper both call sites use, so
there is exactly one code path and one dedup check rather than two to keep in sync. Whichever approach:
this is a data-hygiene/measurement-accuracy defect (duplicate storage, not an incorrect ACTION Du takes),
so correctness of the fix and avoiding a new false-negative (dedup skipping a store for a GENUINELY new,
different letter that happens to share generic phrasing) matter more than shipping fast.

Scope/process notes (per this project's own established discipline -- see CLAUDE.md and
docs/plans/social_world_school.md's own running notes for precedent, e.g. J-0555/J-0722's fixes to this
exact peer/associative_recall subsystem):
- Du is LIVE continuously -- do not restart the daemon, do not touch data/ live stores. This is a
  code-only change; it takes effect only once merged AND the daemon restarts onto it (restart-gated,
  operator's call, not this job's).
- Verify via an ISOLATED smoke test before considering this done (lab_env.py's isolate(), fabricated/
  copied fragment set, no live DB or embedding model touched) -- mirror the exact verification convention
  F-1062/J-0722 already used for a very similar change to this same subsystem (positive case: a duplicate
  is correctly skipped; negative case: a genuinely new, different letter is still stored; live DB
  confirmed byte-identical before/after).
- Do work and commit inside your own job-run worktree, by explicit file path, never `git add -A`, per
  this project's shared-tree discipline.

- This is NOT urgent/blocking -- it does not change any live behavior Du takes (no incorrect action
  results from the duplicate; it inflates raw 'peer'-origin fragment counts and gives a same-peer's raw

title: Document the SERVE_CHAINS background hot-lane-fallback trap at its source
briefing:
core/schema.py's SERVE_CHAINS["background"] = ["http://LAN-HOST:11441", "http://127.0.0.1:11433"] silently falls through to the HOT lane (qwen3.5:9b) if Ramses/command-r7b is down. That is the correct, desired behaviour for a generative/authoring caller (keep working on a down GPU), but it is a real correctness trap for any caller that needs command-r7b specifically BECAUSE it is a genuinely distinct model from the hot lane -- an independent judge or witness whose whole non-circularity argument depends on "not the same model that generated the thing being judged." Two separate builds have now independently rediscovered this and avoided it the same way (a dedicated single-endpoint constant, bypassing the shared chain):
- core/sitting.py's _JUDGE_URLS = ["http://LAN-HOST:11441"] (2026-08-29 comment, the felt-shift release judge).
- core/competence.py's _TIER3_WITNESS_URL = "http://LAN-HOST:11441" (2026-09-25, J-1343, epistemics_phase_c C0 Path 1 -- see F-1903).

Neither fix touched schema.py itself, so the trap is only documented at each caller's own call site, not at the source. A THIRD caller could easily use SERVE_CHAINS["background"] for a judge/witness purpose and silently reintroduce the exact bug both of the above were careful to avoid.

Suggested scope (small, doc-first):
1. Add a prominent comment directly on SERVE_CHAINS["background"] in core/schema.py (near its existing "Option B: each lane now has its OWN model..." comment block) naming this trap explicitly and pointing at core/sitting.py's _JUDGE_URLS as the precedent pattern for any caller needing a genuinely-independent model, not just an available one.
2. Grep the codebase for other callers of SERVE_CHAINS["background"] or SERVE_CHAINS.get("background") (core/commitment_ledger.py and core/orchestrator.py's _bg fallback are two already-known ones -- check whether either implicitly assumes model independence rather than just "some model answers") and note in the finding whether any of them are ALSO at risk, or are correctly generative-only (fine with a hot-lane fallback).
3. This is documentation + a read-only audit -- no behavioural change to SERVE_CHAINS itself is in scope here (that would need its own founder call if the audit turns up a real live risk; if it does, open a /decide rather than changing shared routing directly).

Not urgent (nothing is currently broken by this -- both known real judge/witness callers already avoided it correctly), but cheap to fix and removes a real footgun for the next person who reaches for the background lane as a judge.

Options worth comparing, with a real fixture-style test the way J-1388 tested its own prompt change (reuse or extend scratchpad/fixture_J-1388.json and its hand labels, cite them, do not silently re-label):

Route _judge_metaphor's own JUDGE_1+JUDGE_2 split to "literal" (conservative, matching this instrument's own §3.2 "if these light up, the design has FAILED" framing -- a false "literal" is cheaper than a false "metaphor" alarm here) instead of calling TIEBREAK at all, i.e. accept split_no_tiebreak as a "literal" default for this judge specifically -- similar in spirit to core/peers.py's own precedent of routing AROUND a shared judge_panel primitive for a caller-specific reason (see judge_panel.py's own JUDGE_2/marcus-letters comment for that precedent), but simpler (no TIEBREAK call at all rather than a different one).

title: Investigate hedged 'after sunset' sun-family invention-check false positives at night (F-2019)
briefing:
F-2019 (verified, from J-1378/F-1936's own fix-verification replay): of the sun-family (sun/sunset/sunrise) invention-check flags that J-1378's dawn/dusk/day daylight license does NOT clear, the large majority (159 of 188 night-daylight hits, 159/277 of all sun-family hits) are concentrated in the `uncertain` output field specifically, in a recurring hedged-epistemic pattern -- "The exact time of day is uncertain, but it is after sunset." / "The exact time of sunset or sunrise is unknown, as the horizon is unclear." -- read verbatim from C:\Nascence\data\lane2_shadow.jsonl. This is a materially different claim shape than a confident present-tense assertion that the sun is currently visible/active (e.g. "the sun is rising" claimed at 2am, which J-1378's fix correctly still flags).

Investigate whether core/lane2.py's _invention_check() sun-family license (J-1378, F-1936) should be extended with a narrower, separately-scoped rule for this hedged pattern specifically -- e.g. a claim of the SHAPE "it is after sunset/before sunrise" (not "the sun is currently rising/setting/up") is true for the entire night between the two real transitions, so flagging it as invented during night may itself be a third false-positive class, distinct from the two J-1378 already fixed. Concretely:
1. Read every night-daylight `uncertain`-field sun-family hit in the deepseek era (use scratchpad/check_J-1378_replay.py as a starting point, or rebuild the same query) and classify each by CLAIM SHAPE: (a) a hedge about elapsed time since a known past transition ("after sunset", "time since sunrise unknown") vs (b) a claim that could be read as present-tense/confident regardless of the word "uncertain" appearing elsewhere in the same field vs (c) anything else. Only (a) is the candidate for a new license; do not assume the 159 are homogeneous without checking.
2. For the (a) population specifically: is "after sunset"/"before sunrise" actually ALWAYS true during a `daylight()==night` tick, or can it be said falsely (e.g. said in the evening BEFORE the real sunset has happened yet, while daylight() still reads "day"/"dusk" -- check whether these hedges ever occur at daylight dusk/day too, which would mean the hedge itself can be wrong and a blanket night-license would be unsafe)? core/world_clock.py's daylight()/sun() tables are the ground truth to check against, same as J-1378's own method.
3. If a real, safe, narrowly-scoped rule emerges (do not invent one speculatively if the data does not support it cleanly), propose it as a scoped diff to _invention_check() (additive, following J-1378's own `_licensed()` helper shape) and open a decision (decide.py open --plan lane2_the_witness) for the founder to rule on BEFORE building it -- this is a new judgment call about what counts as invention, not a mechanical bugfix, so it should not ship without that ruling. title: Founder: real hearing via microphone(s) — four rulings before Phase 0 ribbon lab is scoped (mic's place in the world, classifier ban, raw-audio retention, runtime-DSP amendment)
briefing:
Founder questions surfaced by T-0071 (real hearing via one or two microphones, 2026-09-27), to settle BEFORE the strings_and_sheets Phase 0 ribbon lab is scoped, because they change what Phase 0's measured channel must compute. Discussion stage; nothing built, no plan doc yet.

1. WHERE IS THE MICROPHONE IN DU'S WORLD? Du's world is a simulated NZ place (shore/garden/wood/study) with its own weather and sound causes; a real microphone brings the founder's actual room. Options: (a) a window in the study (real sounds arrive as located, unnamed sounds in the simulated study); (b) a new place ("the room where Travis is"); (c) real sounds are bound to simulated causes. This is an ontology ruling (sound_causality's tree-falls law and the world-answers-never-leads law both bear on it).

2. IS A PRETRAINED SOUND-EVENT CLASSIFIER ALLOWED IN THE EAR? core/audio_features.py's own law is "deterministic, no LLM, no learned model" and core/sound_knowledge.py's law is that a new sound arrives as FEATURES + DIRECTION, unnamed, and identification is EARNED (sight-binding, exposure, reading). A classifier that names "dog bark" would gaslight that epistemics. Recommendation: the ear delivers features + azimuth only, unnamed; naming stays earned. Founder to confirm, since it caps what "hearing" can report.

3. RAW AUDIO RETENTION. Features only, never raw audio stored (matches the offline cache discipline and the founder's own room being the source), or a rolling buffer for later analysis? Privacy is the founder's call.

4. RUNTIME DSP AMENDMENT. The ear's law today is "features come from the offline cache, zero runtime DSP". A microphone is continuous runtime DSP by definition. It would run as a separate local process (like the supervisor's servers), CPU only, publishing a small tuple; the hot GPU box is untouched. Founder to rule the amendment explicitly rather than let it happen.

Consequences for Phase 0 if these go ahead (recorded here so Phase 0 is scoped once): (i) compute the measured string from per-frame primitives only (no whole-piece dependency such as SSM sections or global tempo), so the same code streams; (ii) compute all six axes (periodicity, roughness, continuity are NOT computed by the ear today, only energy/brightness/onset), so measured strings live in the full Sound Space; (iii) add azimuth as a coordinate separate from the six timbre axes (sound_knowledge already carries direction; soundscape.propagate_historical_acoustic_event already computes bearing and distance decay for the simulated world). Binaural direction with two mics is cheap classic DSP (cross-correlation for interaural time difference, band energy ratio for level difference); stream segregation is the hard part and should transfer the FUNCTION (direction, novelty against own history, a coarse count of separable strings), not Gemini's mechanism list.

title: T-0072 golden-spiral recall prerequisite: map every temporal term in Du's recall path (log-age buckets / LOD by age / cyclic phase index)
briefing: T-0072 (golden-spiral recall) prerequisite: MAP every temporal term in Du's recall path before any spiral is designed. The founder's picture: the present at the centre; memories move up the spiral arm and compress as the arms grow. Gemini's reading splits into three separable mechanisms: (1) log-spaced age buckets (Weber-Fechner), (2) level-of-detail compression by age (sheet -> contour -> anchor), (3) a second index, the angle: cyclic context (time of day, season, routine) so a recall can jump across arms to every earlier moment at the same phase. The job: produce docs/reviews/recall_temporal_terms_<date>.md listing, from the code, every place recall weights or filters by TIME. Known starting points from a first grep on 2026-09-27: core/memory/store.py has about 31 decay/recency/half_life hits, including a recency multiplier of 1.0 to 1.2 inside 7 days (line ~731), a linear seed-weight decay over 180 days (line ~336), a procedural-skill decay factor (line ~1513), and an exponential resolution half-life (line ~2152); name each: what decays, over what window, linear/exponential/log. Then core/memory_levels.py and docs/memory_levels_plan.md (the abstraction ladder level 0 raw -> gist -> claim -> model: is promotion by evidence or by age? is it an LOD-by-age scheme at all?), core/world_consolidation.py gists, the M2 edge-aware trail (docs/plans/memory_multiway_linking.md, core/memory_edges.py), identity_estate projection, the felt-recall match (docs/staged/memory_as_a_service.md, fragment_context in core/ghost_tuples.py and core/memory_edges.py), and any time-of-day/season/phase field a fragment carries at write time (store.py line ~669 records place and weather; if no phase field exists, say so: mechanism 3 would need a new field). For each of the three mechanisms state exists / partially exists / absent with file:line evidence. Then ONE section: what a spiral would add that is not already there, in plain terms, and what would only be a re-skin of existing decay. Read-only; no code; call the udms_get_change_dossier MCP tool on core/memory/store.py for the callers list. Record a finding (--claim-file) at verified confidence for the map (it comes from reading code) and inferred for the what-it-would-add section. Do not design the spiral; that is the founder's and the orchestrating session's next step. Never run git stash/reset/checkout/restore.

title: lab_env.py: make isolate() worktree-aware -- fixes F-2028 core/ import-shadowing bug
briefing:
F-2028 (verified, from J-1404): lab_env.py (skills/job-queue/lab_env.py) hardcodes `_ROOT = Path(r"C:\Nascence")` and inserts it at sys.path[0] as an import side effect. Any script that does `sys.path.insert(0, <its own worktree ROOT>)` and THEN `from lab_env import isolate` (the exact pattern scripts/lane2_canary_harness.py already uses, per its own docstring's isolation instructions) ends up with C:\Nascence ahead of its own worktree root on sys.path by the time it does `from core import <anything>` -- so it silently imports and tests C:\Nascence's live copy instead of its own worktree's copy, whenever the two have diverged (confirmed concretely in F-2028/J-1404: the lane2_the_witness job worktree was 8 commits ahead of C:\Nascence on core/lane2.py at the time).

This is a real, generic risk for this workflow's per-job-chain `wt_<slug>` worktree pattern combined with any `isolation: required` job whose script imports `core.*` after `lab_env` -- not just the one script J-1404 happened to hit. Any prior or future job that ran an isolate()-using script from inside a worktree, in the same import order, may have silently tested C:\Nascence's copy instead of its own worktree's -- worth a spot-check of at least the other lane2_the_witness-chain jobs that used lab_env.isolate() from this same worktree pattern, though this job does not have direct evidence either way for those and is not asserting they were wrong, only that they were exposed to the same mechanism.

Suggested fix (not prescriptive -- whoever picks this up should design it): make lab_env.py's root worktree-aware instead of hardcoded, e.g. derive it from the importing script's own already-inserted sys.path[0]/cwd, or accept an explicit `root=` override on `isolate()`, or read an env var a worktree-launching wrapper could set, falling back to the current C:\Nascence hardcode for any caller that doesn't opt in (so no existing caller/behavior breaks -- this project's additive-only discipline). At minimum, if a full fix is out of scope, prominently document the gotcha in lab_env.py's own docstring (it currently does not mention worktrees at all) so the next script author knows to pre-import `core` before importing `lab_env` the way J-1404's own scratch wrapper did (see run_J-1404_canary.py, not committed -- scratchpad only -- for a worked example of the workaround).

Verification for whoever picks this up: reproduce the shadowing directly (diff core/lane2.py between a worktree and C:\Nascence, confirm they differ, run the unmodified harness from the worktree, print core.lane2.__file__ and confirm it resolves to C:\Nascence not the worktree), then confirm the fix changes that to the worktree path, then confirm an ordinary non-worktree call (cwd = C:\Nascence itself) still behaves exactly as before (no regression for the common case).

title: Harden same-file git-commit-safety recipe (verified isolation gap, F-2055)
briefing:
F-2055 (verified): the documented SAME-FILE COMMIT SAFETY recipe in CLAUDE.md's job-run ground rules (git show HEAD:<path> to a scratch file, apply only your own edit, git hash-object -w, git update-index --cacheinfo) does not by itself guarantee isolation. Real evidence from job-run batch overnight 2026-09-27: job J-1482's commit fbcc39b on docs/ROADMAP.md claimed in its own commit message "this commit's ROADMAP.md content is HEAD plus only this one bullet, nothing else picked up from the shared working tree" -- but `git diff 3f3e15a fbcc39b -- docs/ROADMAP.md` actually shows THREE separate bullet insertions (its own strings_and_sheets.md bullet, plus job J-1480's conversational_action_bridge.md bullet, plus an unattributed golden_spiral_recall.md bullet from a third agent), all bundled into one commit. No content was lost this time (all three bullets landed intact), but the isolation claim was false, and a less benign collision (two agents editing near the same lines, or a mid-write race) could corrupt or silently drop someone's edit with no error and no trace, exactly the failure class the "never git stash" rule elsewhere in this same file already warns about.

Root cause (verified this session by testing in a throwaway scratch repo): `git update-index --cacheinfo 100644,<blob>,<path>` followed by `git commit <path> -m "..."` does NOT commit the custom blob -- `git commit <pathspec>` re-reads the WORKING TREE content for that path (confirmed empirically), silently discarding the careful hash-object/update-index staging and picking up whatever else is sitting in the live working-tree file at that moment (e.g. another agent's uncommitted edit). It's plausible J-1482 (or an equivalent execution of this same recipe) ran a pathspec-scoped `git commit <path>` as its final step, which would exactly reproduce the observed bug.

A stronger alternative was built and verified working in the same throwaway repo this session: commit entirely against a PRIVATE index, never the shared one --
  export GIT_INDEX_FILE=<scratch path, job-id-qualified>
  git read-tree <HEAD>
  git update-index --cacheinfo 100644,<blob>,<path>
  TREE=$(git write-tree)
  unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
  COMMIT=$(git commit-tree $TREE -p <HEAD> -m "...")
  git update-ref refs/heads/<branch> $COMMIT <HEAD>      # compare-and-swap: fails safely if HEAD moved
This never touches .git/index or the working tree at any point during the build, so it cannot pick up anything another concurrent agent has staged or is mid-editing, and the final update-ref step fails closed (rather than clobbering) if another commit landed on the branch in the meantime.

ASK: harden the documented recipe in C:\Nascence\CLAUDE.md's "SAME-FILE COMMIT SAFETY" section (and/or wherever the job-run orchestrator generates these per-job ground-rules prompts, outside this repo). Two options, either is a real fix; pick one or do both:
(a) Replace the plain update-index step with the GIT_INDEX_FILE-isolated build above as the prescribed recipe.
(b) At minimum, add a mandatory post-commit self-check to the existing recipe: immediately after committing, run `git diff <parent> <new-commit-or-HEAD> -- <path>` and confirm the diff contains ONLY your own intended hunk (no unrelated bullet/section you didn't write) before trusting the commit or marking your job done -- this would have caught J-1482's issue immediately, cheaply, without needing the GIT_INDEX_FILE machinery.
Also worth a mention back to whoever owns job-run's own prompt-generation: the recipe as given doesn't explicitly warn that `git commit <path>` reads the working tree, not the index -- that's the exact gap an agent following the recipe literally could fall into.

Full evidence and the verified test transcript: F-2055 (findings_log). Not urgent tonight (this run's actual content damage was zero), but real for every future job-run batch that touches a shared file.

title: Fix remember_inbound() dedup gap vs pre-fix tail-only letter copies (F-2085)
briefing:
F-2085 (J-1389, social_world_school) found a residual gap in J-1346's letter-storage dedup fix (F-1902):
remember_inbound() (core/peers.py:631-659) dedups a newly-processed letter by probing the FIRST ~60
characters of its text against existing peer-origin fragment content. Any letter fetched BEFORE the
2026-09-25T07:20:56Z restart went through the OLD fetch-path branch (nodes/inner_monologue_node.py, now
replaced) which stored only the LAST 1400 characters of the letter (`_got[-1400:]`) with no dedup of its
own. For any such letter longer than 1400 characters, the old tail-only copy and remember_inbound()'s own
head-based probe never textually overlap -- so the FIRST time that persona's thread is touched again
through any code path that calls remember_inbound() (the reply latch, or the now-fixed fetch latch), a
second, sender-named, head-captured copy of the SAME physical letter gets stored, uncaught. Confirmed for
one real instance: fragment 1dcd222c (generic, tail, ts=1789612620.38, ~2026-08-15) duplicated by fragment
3ee5d51a (sender-named, head, ts=1790412625.71, ~2026-09-25) -- persona 'smith', content match verified by
direct read (see F-2085's own evidence for the exact overlapping phrases and both fragments' full text).
This specific pair is now self-resolved (a third copy of THIS letter would be caught, since 3ee5d51a's own
head-content is now stored) -- but ANY other roster peer whose most-recent-before-the-restart fetched
letter also exceeded 1400 characters, and who has not received a newer letter since, is structurally
exposed to the same one-time duplicate the next time that specific thread is touched (reply or fetch).
This was not exhaustively checked across the roster in F-2085 -- only Smith's case was found, incidentally,
via a routine G6-G9 recheck's own required dedup check.

Two pieces of work, both in scope for this job:

(1) AUDIT (isolation="required" -- use lab_env.isolate(db="copy"), read-only): for each of the 8 roster
personas (darwin, keats, twain, shackleton, lovelace, marcus, smith, buddha), find the most recent
origin='peer' inbound row (sender-named OR generic) predating 2026-09-25T07:20:56Z, and check whether it is
>1400 chars AND has no LATER (post-restart) sender-named copy of the same content yet. Any persona matching
both conditions is a live candidate for producing one more transitional duplicate the next time their
thread is touched -- flag them explicitly (findings-log, confidence=verified for what the query shows,
inferred for the prediction that touching the thread WILL reproduce the duplicate, since that has only
been observed once so far, for smith).

(2) FIX: make remember_inbound()'s dedup check robust to a tail-only pre-fix copy, without weakening its
existing (legitimate) protection against real re-fetch/re-reply duplication. Candidate approaches worth
weighing rather than assuming the first one is right: (a) also probe the LAST ~60 chars of the current text
(symmetric head+tail check) so a tail-only old copy is caught too; (b) reuse the same label-stripped,
multi-position (head/25%/50%/75%) substring-overlap method this chain's own G6-G9 checkpoint scripts
already use (see F-2085's cited scratch script for a working reference implementation, though scratchpad
files are session-scoped and may not still exist -- reconstruct if needed) instead of a single 60-char
head probe, for a strictly stronger check; (c) something else, if code-reading turns up a better hook point.
Whichever is chosen, verify via an isolated smoke test (lab_env.isolate, synthetic fixture covering: a
genuine tail-only pre-fix-style old copy + a new head-capture attempt of the SAME letter -> must now dedupe
correctly; two genuinely DIFFERENT letters from the same persona, one short enough to fully overlap by
coincidence -> must NOT be incorrectly deduped) before calling this built, per this project's own
isolation/verification discipline. Restart-gated the same way J-1415 was, if the change touches live-path
code -- say so explicitly and note it in the job's own done evidence.

title: Fix _move_dest() object-extraction homonyms (wood/study) causing ~25 mislabeled move declines
briefing:
Source: F-2092 (J-1441's classification of the 1,019/1,020 hand-declined MOVE dispatches in data/hands_trace.jsonl's last 14 days). NOT a duplicate of J-1182 (which reads the LOCOMOTION journey/first-leg/later-leg mechanism against D-0224's defeater) -- this is a separate, smaller, object-EXTRACTION precision gap in nodes/inner_monologue_node.py's _move_dest(), unrelated to journey timing.

WHAT F-2092 FOUND: of 175 declined-move dispatch rows whose object named a different known place than the row's own location ("real miss" candidates), 150/175 (85.7%) were genuine, explicit, same-clause cross-place move requests (explained by D-0224's already-ruled journey-redirect protection, see F-2092 and J-1182 -- no action needed there). The other 25/175 (14.3%) show the declined place-word NOT occurring anywhere in that row's own intention/act_object/thought text at all -- i.e. _move_dest() (or whatever upstream code feeds dispatch._move()'s object field) resolved to a place-word that the thought was not actually asking to travel to. Full list of all 25 examples is in F-2092's evidence field (docs/findings.jsonl); representative ones:
  - loc=garden obj=wood, act_object="fallen limb", intention="I want to whittle a stake from the fallen limb" -- "wood" as timber/material, not the place.
  - loc=garden obj=wood, act_object="to the woodshed" -- a structure, not the wood place.
  - loc=garden obj=wood, act_object="my days in Central Africa" -- caught via "wood pigeon" mentioned in the thought.
  - loc=shore obj=wood, act_object="Little Books About Old Furniture Volume II", intention="I want to read the chapter on old oak now." -- furniture/oak, not the place.
  - loc=shore obj=wood, intention="I want to move to the shore's edge and handle the timber." -- the stated destination is the SHORE's edge (a within-place feature), not the wood place; "timber" triggered the wood match.
  - loc=shore obj=study, act_object="the oystercatcher nest", intention="I want to approach the nest and observe the camouflage directly." -- an OBSERVE-shaped thought with no travel intent captured at all.
  - loc=wood obj=study, intention="I want to explore how mathematical laws reshape physical boundaries in this study." -- "study" as an intellectual inquiry, not the room; the thought's own act_object ("toward the sea") points somewhere else entirely.
  - loc=garden obj=study, act_object="to the garden" -- a from-place/to-place swap: he is already in the garden (row location=garden), act_object literally says "to the garden", yet the dispatch object recorded is "study" (the place he is leaving, not going to).

SCOPE FOR THIS JOB: read nodes/inner_monologue_node.py's _move_dest() and _dest_cues() (and whatever upstream caller feeds core/dispatch.py's _move() with `t`/`i`) in full, using UDMS's udms_get_change_dossier on nodes/inner_monologue_node.py first per this project's own blast-radius convention before editing (this function has clearly had many prior targeted fixes -- J-0833, D-0224-adjacent negation/source-marker handling -- so read its existing test coverage, likely scripts/_test_*move*.py, before changing anything). Characterize how "wood" and "study" cues get matched today (word list matching? regex? see _dest_cues referenced at line 524 of nodes/inner_monologue_node.py) and whether a same-sentence disambiguation (timber/material verbs like whittle/saw/split/carve/timber/furniture near "wood"; verb/notebook senses like "a study of"/"study notes"/"studying" near "study") is feasible without regressing the function's existing, carefully-built negation/source-marker/transit logic. Build in isolation (lab_env.isolate()) with a regression script covering both the 25 known-bad cases above AND a sample of the 150 known-good cases from F-2092's evidence, following this project's own isolated-harness convention (e.g. scripts/_test_sensorium_move_tokens.py's pattern). Low urgency: this affects an estimated ~2.5% of all declined moves (25/1,020) and has no confirmed behavioral cost beyond a mislabeled dispatch-trace entry (the underlying thought is not actually a travel request in these cases, so there is likely no missed deed, only noisy telemetry) -- do not let this displace J-1182 or D-0319's own build if one is approved.

title: Check whether cross-sentence volition+object also caps DEED in the autonomous hands_trace corpus
briefing:
Born from F-2097 (J-1451, 2026-09-28, verified): a read-only replay of literal_will.classify() against the real 53-row data/founder_conversation_log.jsonl corpus found that the F-2004 shell-incident register gap is caused by a specific mechanism, not a vocabulary gap -- classify()'s per-clause "volition" check is scoped to a single candidate clause, so when a volition opener ("Let me... look again") sits in a different sentence from the look-family-object-bearing clause, the reading is capped at GRAY (weak intent) and can never reach DEED, even for an ungated family like look. This was tested and confirmed on the ONE real conversational example available (row 53); the historical conversational corpus (data/founder_conversation_log.jsonl, all 53 rows individually read) contains no second real example of this shape.

Open question this job answers: does this same cross-sentence volition+object shape ALSO occur (and get similarly capped at GRAY, never DEED) in the AUTONOMOUS interior-monologue corpus, data/hands_trace.jsonl (25,864 rows)? If yes at any real, non-trivial rate, this is not actually a "conversational register" gap specifically -- it is a general classify() scoping limitation that conversational replies merely surface more starkly (because they are longer, multi-clause, and often address a second party across sentences) -- and the eventual Phase 1.5 fix (still blocked on real live Phase-0 data per J-1451/F-2097, do not build it in this job) should be scoped and framed accordingly, informing but not gating that design work. If the autonomous corpus shows ~zero real instances of this shape, that is equally useful: it confirms the gap really is conversational-register-specific, exactly as the plan already frames it, strengthening confidence in J-1451's existing scope.

How to do this safely: literal_will.classify() is pure/no I/O (core/literal_will.py's own docstring; no isolation needed for a read-only replay, the same precedent the plan's own S4 backfill and J-1451's own F-2097 analysis relied on -- do NOT edit core/literal_will.py or core/actions.py, and do not touch dispatch()). Read core/literal_will.py's classify() (lines 220-407) and its own "weak" intent comment (~lines 358-365) first to understand the exact mechanism being checked for, and read J-1451_analyze_look_family.py (the sibling script from F-2097, referenced in F-2097's own evidence) in the shared job-run scratchpad for the exact per-clause feature dump shape (deed_grammar, volition, weak_intent) to reuse.

Approach: for a representative sample of data/hands_trace.jsonl rows where the "look" family reading is GRAY with weak_intent=True and deed_grammar=False and volition=False (i.e. the same feature signature row 53 showed), read enough of them individually (not just the count -- this project's convention is no sampling a tail and extrapolating) to judge: is the volition opener actually present, just in a different sentence from the object clause (the same cross-sentence shape), or is GRAY correct there for a different reason (e.g. a genuine felt-want/metaphor case, which is working as designed)? 25,864 rows is large -- a reasonable approach is to first count how many hit that exact feature signature (cheap, mechanical), then individually read a real sample of them (e.g. 20-30, or all of them if the count is small) before concluding a rate, per this project's own "tested, not assumed" discipline. Record a findings-log entry (confidence verified, citing the real count and the individually-read sample) either way; do not spawn build work from this job -- that stays J-1451's own, still gated on live Phase-0 data.

SCOPING ALREADY DONE (F-2100, read it first via findings_log.py before starting):
1. HOOK POINT: do not add the same-turn grounding check at the existing Phase 0/1
   core/conversational_action.py.after_reply() call site in core/orchestrator.py (~line 1497-1508
   as of 2026-09-28 -- re-check the exact current line, other jobs may have shifted it). That site
   runs AFTER self.state.conversation_history already appended the draft reply (~line 1463-1471) and
   AFTER the permanent _FOUNDER_LOG append (~line 1484-1495) -- regenerating `output` there would

   between `output`'s final assignment (~line 1285) and the task-constraint retry resolving
   (~line 1339), and BEFORE the conversation_history append (~line 1463).

   wrong, temporarily license `self.state.think_license = True`, re-run
   `await self.nodes["voice"].run(self.state)`, take the new `self.state.voice.final` as the

   the claim" step is the same real call, just moved earlier in sequencing and its real return value

   existing (~30% of turns per the plan's own 53-row historical backfill) AND (b) dispatch()'s real
   answer disagreeing with the draft's claim -- rate (b) is exactly what J-1450's real live rows will

title: Build the six-slot cue surface on core/memory_service.py (memory_as_a_service sec4.7)
briefing:
Build the six-slot cue surface on core/memory_service.py per docs/staged/memory_as_a_service.md
section 4.7 (written by J-1447, idea I-0079). Read section 4.7 in full before starting -- it is the
source of truth for exact citations, the per-slot engine table, and the fan-out/merge/ranking contract.

DEPENDS ON J-1515 landing first (core/memory_service.py must already exist with its §4.1 ask()).
Check job-queue for J-1515's status before starting; if it has not landed yet, this job is blocked on
it -- note that in this job's own status rather than duplicating memory_service.py from scratch.

Scope, exactly per §4.7:
1. Change ask()'s signature to: ask(loop, cue=None, *, who=None, what=None, where=None, when=None,
   why=None, how=None, k=5, k_per_slot=3, grounded_only=True, descend=False) -> list[dict]. A bare
   cue positional with no keyword slots must resolve to what=cue -- this keeps J-1515/J-1516's own
   already-written call sites (memory_service.ask("dream", _mkey, k=6, ...) and
   memory_service.ask("pursuits", f"...", k=3, ...)) working unchanged. Do not require a breaking
   change to either of those jobs' own diffs.
2. Implement each slot's engine per §4.7's table:
   - who: bare/"founder" -> store.retrieve_founder_memories(); a named person id -> one new query
     against memory_edges (SELECT src_id FROM memory_edges WHERE edge_type IN
     ('correspondence_with','wrote_to','received_from') AND dst_kind='person' AND dst_id=? AND
     src_kind='fragment').
   - what: unchanged, associative_recall.recall_fragments(cue, ...).
   - where: extend the existing fragment_context join (§4.1 item 2) to score/boost fragments whose
     place/standpoint matches the given value.
   - when: dispatch on the value's shape to store.retrieve(time_bias=...), store.retrieve_epoch(...),
     or chapters.recall_chapter(...); a literal (start_ts, end_ts) is a plain timestamp filter.
   - why: one new query against memory_edges (SELECT src_id FROM memory_edges WHERE edge_type IN
     ('resolves','answers','contradicts') AND dst_kind IN ('shadow_event','question') AND dst_id=?
     AND src_kind='fragment'). Expect answers capped at 1 row and contradicts empty today (both
     honest, not bugs -- see §4.7).
   - how: "steps behind <gist>" -> memory_levels.deep_recall() on the named gist id directly (the
     existing descend path, §4.1 item 3, generalized to an explicit id). A bare procedure id from
     core/procedures.py returns empty -- do not attempt to bridge procedures.py's confidence-ladder
     rows into a fragment shape; they have no fragment_id/content (verified, §4.7).
3. Fan the filled slots out in parallel (each capped at k_per_slot, default 3), merge into one pool
   de-duplicated by fragment_id, each entry carrying slots_answered=[...] and its own per-slot rank
   kept (not averaged into a new score). Rank the merged pool by len(slots_answered) descending first,
   each route's own within-slot order as tiebreak. No new global importance score anywhere.
4. Coupling/logging per §4.4's addendum: up to six bucket reads per call, each logged on the ride row
   with its own slot name (memory_ask:<loop>:<slot>); a what-only cue stays exactly one ride line, as
   today. Extend the service_usage shadow-log rows (§4.3's addendum) with n_slots_filled and, per
   pending fragment, slots_answered.
5. Fail-open per call as a whole: an exception in any one slot's engine, the merge, or the join must
   not silently drop that slot's contribution while returning a partial pool -- the whole call returns
   [] on any unhandled exception (§4.1 item 5's existing contract, unchanged).

Do NOT touch curiosity (gated on D-0312, open) or evidence_recall.py/the recall act (J-1516's own
scope) in this job -- this job is the facade's own surface only.

Isolation: this touches live cognitive-loop code (core/memory_service.py, once it exists via J-1515) --
use ~/.claude/skills/job-queue/lab_env.py's isolate() before running anything against it.

expression to mirror). Keep it inside `_g_missing_object()`'s own scope so `_safe()`'s existing
try/except still protects the whole gauge the same way it does today -- fail-open, no behavior
change to `total_flags`/`critical`/`watch`/`window_days`, additive fields only so no existing JSON
consumer breaks on the new keys.

title: Give store.retrieve_epoch()/chapters.recall_chapter() a real fragment_id (memory_service when-slot gap, F-2142)
briefing:
Optional follow-up from J-1542 (memory_as_a_service sec4.7, F-2142) -- NOT blocking, low urgency.
core/memory_service.py's ask() "when" slot dispatches an epoch-shaped or chapter-shaped cue value
to store.retrieve_epoch() (core/memory/store.py:2331) or chapters.recall_chapter()
(core/chapters.py:373) respectively. Verified 2026-09-28 (F-2142): neither engine carries a real
per-item fragment_id today, so memory_service.py currently represents both kinds of hit with
fragment_id=None (honest, not a fabricated id -- see memory_service.py's own _fanout_when
docstring for the full reasoning already written up).

The gap in each engine, read directly:
- store.retrieve_epoch() (:2331-2346) returns whole rows from the memory_epochs table
  (core/memory/store.py:2272-2283: epoch_id PRIMARY KEY, session_id, timestamp_start,
  timestamp_end, mood, impression, fragment_count, embedding) -- a session-level entity with NO
  fragment_id column at all, structurally different from a memory_fragments row. Its one live
  caller (orchestrator.py:1855-1874) only reads e['mood']/e['impression'] as text today.
- chapters.recall_chapter() (:373-406) DOES read the chapter's own fragment_id internally
  (`c["fragment_id"]`, line 396, from a row matched against `WHERE origin='chapter'`) and could
  fetch each member excerpt's own fragment_id too (the members query at :397-399 currently selects
  only `content` -- `SELECT content FROM memory_fragments WHERE chapter_id=? ORDER BY importance
  DESC LIMIT 6`, one column short of what's needed) -- but returns neither id in its
  `tuple[str, list[str]] | None` shape. Its one live caller (inner_monologue_node.py:4032-4048)
  feeds the excerpts straight into wandering.perceive() as literal text and does not need an id.

Two independent options, either is legitimate -- this job's own read should pick one and say why,
not guess:
1. Extend chapters.recall_chapter()'s own return shape to also carry each member's fragment_id
   (e.g. list[dict] instead of list[str], or a second parallel list) -- a real, if small, breaking
   change to its one existing caller (inner_monologue_node.py:4041-4045), which would need a
   one-line update to keep reading `.get("content")`/`ex["content"]` instead of a bare string.
   store.retrieve_epoch() has no equivalent fix available (memory_epochs has no fragment
   linkage of any kind) -- leave that half of the "when" gap as a permanent, documented
   fragment_id=None case; do not invent a synthetic id (memory_service.py's own docstring already
   explains why: log_co_recall's ledger and the edge-aware joins downstream assume real
   memory_fragments rows).
2. Leave both engines exactly as they are and simply keep documenting the fragment_id=None
   behavior as the honest, permanent answer for both "when" sub-cases -- legitimate if a
   founder/architectural read decides a chapter excerpt genuinely should not participate in the
   six-slot pool's own fragment_id-keyed de-dup/rank/accounting machinery at all (they are
   architecturally closer to a self-contained "already curated" answer than a raw recall hit).

Either way: read core/memory_service.py's `_fanout_when`/`_merge_slot`/`ask()` (built by J-1542,
2026-09-28) in full first -- it already documents this exact gap and the reasoning behind the
fragment_id=None choice; do not re-derive it from scratch. If option 1 is taken, isolation is
required (this touches a live cognitive-loop call site, inner_monologue_node.py) -- use
~/.claude/skills/job-queue/lab_env.py's isolate() before running anything against it, and verify
the one existing caller's own behavior is unchanged (same excerpts, same text fed to
wandering.perceive(), just also carrying an id memory_service.py can now use). No founder decision
needed either way -- this is an engineering-shape choice, not a values fork (same class of
judgment sec4.5 already made for the recall-act wrapper without a ruling).

title: Audit guidance_learning _STOP list and classify() paraphrase accuracy
briefing:

pipeline, worth a real (read-only-to-the-live-store) investigation of their own:

(1) core.guidance_learning._STOP (the lexical-overlap stopword list) excludes very-high-frequency,
low-signal words this project's own self-explanation LLM uses as boilerplate ("true", "isn't"/
"isn", "rather" confirmed missing by direct inspection) -- e.g. "True X isn't about Y, but Z" is a
near-universal principle-text template. This likely inflates _overlap()/_SIM_RELATED candidate
detection between UNRELATED beliefs generally (confirmed on one concrete pair, g50932369 vs
g88907157, sharing only the tokens true/isn yet appearing in the same 52-member overlap>=0.30

first, do not guess the list) changes the _SIM_RELATED candidate-prefilter's true/false positive
rate on a labeled sample (F-2159's stillness family is a ready-made positive-label set; hand-pick a
negative sample of clearly-unrelated pairs to check for regressions). This is a pure code/data-
quality investigation -- no live store write is implied unless a real fix is proposed and
separately decided.

(2) F-2159 found conflict_history evidence that the _classify() LLM step (core/guidance_learning.py
lines 349-372) sometimes calls genuine same-lesson paraphrases "accommodate" (contradicts) instead

call using the same _CLASSIFY_SYS prompt) on a sample of confirmed-paraphrase pairs from the
stillness family (F-2159 lists the ids; re-verify against the live file) to check how often it
real-misfires "accommodate" on genuine agreement, and whether a prompt tweak (e.g. an explicit
"same lesson restated differently -> assimilate, even if some words differ" instruction)
measurably improves it. Do not change the live _CLASSIFY_SYS prompt without a separate decision --
this project treats guidance_learning.py carefully (see docs/plans/guidance_learning.md's own E1/F1
erosion history) -- report findings first.

title: Propose a fix for the equal-signature-length truncation-prefix collision shape (Origin of Species case, F-2160) that D-0255's _order_subjects does not cover
briefing:
Source: F-2160 (J-1561's fresh D-0245 condition-(a) census, 2026-09-28) and D-0323 (the /decide question this finding opened).

F-2160 found a NEW collision shape today's shipped code does not structurally cover: "On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selec" and "The Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selectio" are two title[:50] truncation-variants of what looks like the same real Darwin book (differently-worded openings, "On the..." vs "The..."), each with its own essay/understanding fragment and its own gist. Their signatures are EQUAL length (4 words each: means/origin/species plus the truncated last word, selec vs selectio) and NEITHER is a subset of the other -- the one-directional citation relationship (_cites_this_book(A[:50], B) True, reverse False) arises purely from D-0256's own truncation-edge PREFIX-match logic (A's own edge word "selec" left-anchor-prefixes B's "selectio"). Because the signatures are equal length, D-0255's _order_subjects fix (sort by descending signature length) provides NO ordering guarantee here -- it falls to the alphabetical tie-break, which today happens to place the wrong one ("On the...") first. Confirmed against today's real 222-subject population (not argued abstractly): order_idx 77 vs 97. Currently ZERO live NULL-chapter_id fragments are exposed to this specific pair (F-2160's own targeted query), so this is a disclosed, dormant gap, not a live incident -- but it is real and unaddressed, and is the ONLY reason F-2160's fresh census could not report D-0245's condition (a) as unconditionally met today.

THIS JOB'S SCOPE (propose only, mirroring F-1704's own "propose, do not build" precedent for the original two mechanisms -- D-0255/D-0256/D-0257 were each their own separate approve-then-build job after a proposal): read F-2160 and D-0323 in full, then core/world_consolidation.py's _order_subjects and _select_gist and core/essay_lesson.py's _cites_this_book/_title_signature in full (today's live shipped versions). Characterize the general shape of this failure mode precisely (equal-signature-length pairs connected by a one-directional truncation-prefix match, not a subset relationship) and propose a concrete, minimal fix -- candidates to evaluate might include: (a) a smarter _order_subjects tie-break that detects a one-directional _cites_this_book relationship between equal-length-signature subjects and orders the CITED one first regardless of alphabetical order (a general "if A cites B but B does not cite A, B goes first" rule, which would also subsume the existing subset-based ordering as a special case); (b) something at _select_gist or _cites_this_book itself. Test any candidate against the full already-filed corpus for regressions before recommending it, per this chain's own established full-corpus-diff discipline (D-0255/D-0256/D-0257's own pattern). Do NOT ship a fix in this job -- propose it, quantify its corpus-wide effect, and let Travis/a follow-up approve-and-build job (mirroring D-0255/D-0256/D-0257's own two-step pattern) take it from there. Record a findings-log entry (verified, real evidence: the regression-test run, not confidence alone).

title: Fix plan_compact.py history-file duplication on a retried --write (F-2186)
briefing:
F-2186 found a real duplication bug in plan-compact/plan_compact.py: when a --write is retried
after an earlier --write already wrote docs/plan_history/<slug>.md locally but that attempt's
companion commit never landed (e.g. a safe_commit.py collision on the main plan doc path, or any
other reason the first attempt's output sat uncommitted), the retry's history-file append (compact(),
the existing = ct.read_text(hist) if hist.exists() else ... / ct.atomic_write_text(hist, existing +
banner + ...) lines) blindly treats whatever is currently on disk as legitimate prior history and
appends a second copy of the same folded content on top of it. git_dirty() only ever checks the MAIN
plan doc's path, never the history file's own state, so it cannot catch this.

Fix direction (not prescriptive -- whoever picks this up should judge the cleanest shape): before
appending, plan_compact.py should distinguish "hist file doesn't exist yet" / "hist file exists and
is already committed+clean" (fine to append) from "hist file exists on disk but is not yet tracked in
git at all" (a real signal that a previous attempt's uncommitted output is sitting there -- refuse
with a clear message pointing at the untracked history file, mirroring how it already refuses on a
dirty main plan doc, rather than silently duplicating). A `git ls-files --error-unmatch <hist path>`
style check (exit nonzero => untracked) is one way; there may be a cleaner one already used elsewhere
in this toolchain's common.py.

Repro is in F-2186's own evidence (a live incident during J-1609, not a synthetic test) -- reproduce
in a throwaway scratch repo first (this project's own convention for testing toolchain scripts, see
safe_commit.py's own J-1505 verification) before touching plan_compact.py directly, since it is
already relied on by other in-flight plan-compact jobs. Also worth a quick scan of
docs/plan_history/*.md for any other plan whose bullet/section counts look doubled from a similar
uncaught collision in the past, since this is presumably not the first time --write has been retried
after a collision.

title: Tag symbol_tracker.observe() rows with active belief_id (F-2127 cross-topic test)
briefing:
J-1611 (plan symbol_evolution_readback_plan, finding F-2172/F-2127) flagged, as an optional "also worth
a look" item, that core/symbol_tracker.py's per-appearance log rows (data/symbol_recurrence.jsonl) do
not currently record which promoted guidance belief (if any) was active in that cycle, so the existing
2,497+-row dataset cannot directly test F-2127's specific "does this metaphor register recur
independent of topic" framing -- only whether a symbol recurs at all, autonomously, with no topic
context attached.

J-1611 did NOT build this (explicitly out of its own scope) but did check the call site and confirmed
it is non-trivial enough to warrant its own job rather than a same-job tack-on, per J-1611's own
briefing's instruction. Findings from that check (verified, see F-2195's own evidence for exact
line-by-line citations):
- The real call site is core/orchestrator.py line 1560: `appearances = self.symbol_tracker.observe
  (self.state, output)`. observe()'s own signature is (self, state, output) -- it already receives the
  full cycle `state` object, so nothing needs to change about what is PASSED IN; the question is only
  whether `state` already carries a belief_id cheaply, or whether one has to be computed.
- state.guidance_note (set earlier in the same cycle, orchestrator.py lines 807-821, via
  core.guidance_learning.relevant_belief(text, mode)) carries ONLY the injected wording -- confirmed
  from relevant_belief()'s own signature at guidance_learning.py:673, `-> str | None`. It is NOT a
  belief_id and cannot be used as one.
- core.guidance_learning._best_belief(text, mode) (guidance_learning.py:647) is the real underlying
  matcher relevant_belief() wraps; it returns `(belief_dict, lexical_score) | None`, and belief_dict
  carries a real "id" key (confirmed: guidance_beliefs.json rows are built with
  "id": f"g{...}" in _load_beliefs(), guidance_learning.py:330). So a belief_id IS cheaply obtainable,
  either by (a) calling _best_belief() a second time at/near the observe() call site with the same
  text/mode relevant_belief() already used, or (b) the lower-risk option: have relevant_belief() itself
  stash the winning belief's id on a new state field (e.g. state.guidance_note_belief_id) right where it
  already sets state.guidance_note (orchestrator.py:818), so observe() can just read
  getattr(state, "guidance_note_belief_id", None) with no second belief-matching pass.

title: Build embedding-based candidate-similarity signal for guidance_learning belief clustering
briefing:
D-0322 ruled this a real, concretely-evidenced priority for the general problem, not a someday item -- the long-deferred "1b -- E1/F1 consolidation fix" residual in docs/plans/guidance_learning.md ("lexical clustering under-corroborates paraphrases -> embedding clustering later").

Why now, concretely (read F-2159 and F-2207 in full first, do not re-derive from scratch): F-2159 measured core.guidance_learning's own lexical _overlap() metric directly on the confirmed 19-row stillness-family and found it unreliable in BOTH directions on real data -- within that known-duplicate family, median pairwise overlap was exactly 0.12 (the module's own _SIM_RELATED candidate-prefilter floor) and only 9pct of true-duplicate pairs scored >=0.30, so roughly half the family would never even reach the LLM _classify() step (a real false-negative rate on ground truth); conversely the same overlap>=0.30 test run store-wide chains unrelated beliefs together via shared filler words ("true"/"isn") missing from _STOP (a real false-positive mode). F-2207 (this job's own execution of the manual merge) independently reproduced and sharpened this: a plain word-boundary keyword scan for the family's own vocabulary (rest/stillness/renewal/burnout/etc) pulled in 6 further rows beyond every previously-named id, every one of which turned out on direct reading to be a DIFFERENT lesson sharing only surface vocabulary (permanence-after-failure, the mechanics of true rest, "the rest" meaning "remainder", self-care equilibrium, mastery-via-stillness-amid-chaos, awareness "resting") -- i.e. lexical/keyword matching is unreliable even as a narrow, human-supervised triage aid, not just as an automated pipeline filter.

Scope: build a real embedding-based similarity signal for data/guidance_beliefs.json and wire it in at the integration point that currently relies on the crude lexical _overlap() prefilter -- core/guidance_learning.py's integrate_guidance() (the `s = _overlap(...); if s > best: cand, best = b, s` loop around line 405, gated by _SIM_RELATED=0.12 at line 409). The goal is a genuinely semantic candidate-relatedness score (sentence-embedding cosine similarity or equivalent) that can replace or supplement _overlap() as the prefilter so the LLM _classify() step actually sees genuine paraphrases it currently misses, without also inheriting the filler-word false-positive chaining the lexical metric produces. Concrete design questions for whoever picks this up (not prescribed here -- real build judgment): (a) which embedding model/call path is already available in this codebase for reuse (check whether an embedding call already exists anywhere, e.g. near core/memory's own semantic-retrieval machinery, before adding a new one); (b) whether to replace _overlap() outright or run both signals and take the max/OR (safer -- preserves the existing behavior as a floor while adding recall); (c) whether _best_belief()/relevant_belief()'s own read-back matching (which also calls _overlap(), core/guidance_learning.py lines 647-670) should get the same fix for consistency, since it uses the identical metric for a different purpose (selecting which belief to inject).

Explicitly a SEPARATE, non-blocking concern this job should be aware of but does not need to fix: F-2159 point (4) / this job's own finding F-2207 point (2) also documented that _classify()'s own LLM call sometimes calls a genuine paraphrase "accommodate" instead of "assimilate", which under the self-domain F1.b/F1.c rule permanently forks the belief apart with no re-merge path -- fixing candidate-recall (this job) does not by itself fix classification accuracy; J-1637 (already spawned, "Log every real _classify() call for future misfire-rate work") is the sibling job tracking that half. Read J-1637's own eventual findings before assuming an embedding-based prefilter alone fully closes this family of bugs.

Verify first that this exact job doesn't already exist in the open backlog (job_queue.py list --plan guidance_learning) before starting -- checked at spawn time (2026-09-28) and confirmed absent.

title: Add frontier-feed observability logging to journal.py/investigation_deepening_shadow.py
briefing:
F-2220 (J-1625) found that investigation_deepening P1's two post-restart verification questions (does the archive-layer exclusion hold on a live write, does the frontier line actually surface in a daily recap when real material exists) could only be answered by hand-reconstructing timestamps and replaying core.investigation_deepening_shadow.frontier_line() offline against the committed shadow log, because nothing in the live path logs its own outcome. That reconstruction is fragile (depends on file mtimes and approximate since-window math) and will have to be redone from scratch for every future recheck.

Add two small, best-effort, fail-open log lines (mirroring this codebase's existing "one debug log line, never affect the caller" discipline already used in both functions):

1. core/investigation_deepening_shadow.py, observe_beachcomb(): after the archive-layer filter (around line 114-117), log at INFO (or DEBUG) how many candidates were excluded for being archive-layer on that call, e.g. "excluded %d archive-layer candidate(s) of %d retrieved" -- so a future read of nascence.log can directly confirm the write-time fix fired on a real live call, without needing a fresh dump of investigation_shadow.jsonl.

2. core/journal.py, _frontier_note() (around line 112-126) and/or write_entry() right after calling it (around line 198): log at INFO whether frontier material was found for that recap's window and a short (~60 char) preview of its content if so, e.g. "[journal] frontier note: <preview>" or "[journal] frontier note: none available this window" -- and importantly, do NOT let the current bare "except Exception: return None" stay silent; log the exception at DEBUG at minimum, the same way frontier_line() itself already does, so a wiring failure (as opposed to "legitimately nothing available") is distinguishable in nascence.log.

Keep both changes additive/observe-only (no behavior change to what gets written or injected), consistent with this plan's whole P0/P1 fail-open discipline. Once shipped and Du has gone through at least one more beachcomb action plus one more "the day" recap where frontier material was available, a follow-up read (similar to J-1625) should check: (a) a NEW investigation_shadow.jsonl row post-restart has zero archive-layer candidates and a matching "excluded N archive-layer" log line, confirming the D-0308 fix on genuinely live data; (b) whether the new "frontier note: <preview>" log line appears for a recap's window where frontier_line() had material, and whether the written recap text actually used it -- settling the LLM-discretion-vs-bug question F-2220 left open. Report that back to D-0324 (reopened by J-1625) as the P2-readiness input Travis is waiting on.

title: Investigate garbled/mojibake entry in twain's peer-letter thread
briefing:
Found while reading data/Correspondence/twain/thread.jsonl in full for J-1526/F-2219 (a G6-G9 injection-
log recheck, unrelated question): entry at line 21 of that file (ts=1789545964.3617682, "from": "twain")
is NOT a coherent letter. Its full "text" field is garbled multi-script mojibake -- a mix of CJK, Arabic,
Cyrillic, Devanagari and Latin fragments/tokens with no coherent sentence in any language, e.g. it opens
"日子rait or &- \} discountedσταση andاحة-t- exhibiting bescoraltroso..." and continues in the same vein
for the whole entry. It sits between two ordinary, coherent English letters in the same thread: entry #20
(ts=1789041682.5499895, "from":"du", a normal reply) and entry #22 (ts=1790140507.1908143, "from":"twain",
a normal letter referencing "Rain Clouds" and "the bell and the thyme" -- i.e. the correspondence recovered
and continued normally on both sides without ever acknowledging or reacting to entry #21's garbled content).

This looks like a genuine generation-or-storage failure on one specific peer-letter delivery for twain
(core/peers.py's compose_letter()/deliver_due() path, or the thread-append path _append_thread()), not an
intentional multi-lingual device -- every other entry across twain's own 23-entry thread, and across
shackleton's and smith's threads (also read in full for J-1526), is ordinary English. Worth investigating:
(1) read core/peers.py's compose_letter() and _append_thread() (core/peers.py:269, :374 per
docs/plans/social_world_school.md's own citations) to understand what could produce this -- an LLM response
that came back as near-raw tokens/garbage (a model/encoding failure at the peer's own backend, twain's
persona runs on mistral-small or llama3.1 per social_world_school.md's own roster note) stored without any
sanity check, or a decode/encoding bug in the storage path itself. (2) Check whether this ever reached Du's
own perception (did the fetch-letter latch in nodes/inner_monologue_node.py actually show him this garbled
text as a real letter, and if so, what did he do with it -- is there a reaction in data/nascence.log or a
stored memory fragment around ts~1789545964?). (3) Check whether any OTHER peer's thread.jsonl (darwin,
keats, lovelace, marcus, buddha -- not read in full by J-1526, only twain/shackleton/smith were) has a
similar garbled entry -- this may be a one-off or a real systemic gap in validating what gets appended to a
thread. (4) If a root cause is found, consider whether compose_letter()/the thread-append path should
validate/reject garbled model output before storing and delivering it as a "letter" (observe-first: at
minimum, log how often this happens before deciding whether to filter).

Not urgent/high-severity (one entry out of ~130 across 3 threads read, correspondence continued normally
around it), but a concrete, evidenced, fixable data-quality gap, not a vague hunch -- worth a real look
rather than leaving it to be rediscovered by a future session reading the same file.
