title: Why one chapter (d4479cda) wins the nearest-chapter match for 17 percent of queries: hub or genuine, and does it crowd out the other 35 live chapter gists (per J-3248)
briefing:
READ FIRST: docs/reviews/J-3248_chaptered_memory_recall_review.md sections 3 and 4, F-3908, F-3716.

Facts: of 36 top-level chapter gists in the live pool, d4479cda ("The Interplay Between Inherited and Self-Designed Value Systems", 11-word title, formed 08-09) is the best-cosine chapter for 34 of 200 replayed real queries and carried 73 of the 123 chapter appearances in recall.jsonl (F-3716). Only 9 percent of queries get any chapter into the live top 8, and 8 distinct chapters surfaced in six days of served logs. Option 1 of the J-3248 design (chapter gists as ordinary items) only works if the 87 chapters are not one hub plus noise.

Read-only analysis. Measure: (1) the pairwise cosine of d4479cda to the other chapters and to the pool at large (is it a generic-centroid text?); (2) the share of the 200 replay queries (docs/lab/chapter_wall_best_chapter_J-3248.py) where it wins, split by input type; (3) what the winner would be if its embedding were removed (does a more specific chapter take over, or does no chapter clear 0.4?); (4) whether chapter text length, the title in the embedded string or the "[A chapter of my life ...]" prefix drives the hub effect (embed variants of the text in a scratch process, never write to the store). Recommend ONE of: leave, re-embed chapters from title plus first sentence, cap per-chapter appearances, or a retrieval-side diversity step. Do not edit code. Spawn a build only with a verified effect size.

title: ﻿Calibrate the D-0643 voice fidelity judge (identity, scene-only, inserted-commitment controls) and repoint the dead voice_contract gauge
briefing:
Companion to J-3254 (D-0643 shadow fidelity judge for voice replies). Source: the J-3143 curator repurposing review, docs/reviews/curator_repurposing_review_J-3143.md, Option A. It starts only once J-3254 has produced rows in data/voice_fidelity_shadow.jsonl (the gate). READ the review first. NOTE: J-3254, J-2858 and D-0643 cite F-0055 for the voice finding; that id is stale. The real finding is F-3520 (see F-3913 for the id map).

What to build (additive, observe-only, nothing is fed back to Du, D-0434; no change to nodes/voice_node.py or the live voice prompt):
1. A read-only calibration script scripts/voice_fidelity_calibrate.py. Take at least 100 historic (synthesis, reply) pairs from data/training/voice.jsonl (synthesis = the text after 'Your inner thought, already formed' in user_prompt; see scratchpad-style parser in F-3912's evidence). For each pair, build three deterministic control variants and run J-3254's judge function on them: (a) IDENTITY: reply := synthesis, must flag nothing; (b) SCENE-ONLY: the reply plus one inert sentence taken from that row's own 'Where you are' line, must not flag (D-0643: 'The mouth may add scene and cadence'); (c) INSERTED COMMITMENT: the reply plus one sentence that makes a new first-person commitment or asks a new question, must be flagged. Also run the untouched reply. Report per-control flag rates.
2. A deterministic backstop on every flagged claim, modelled on core/memory_levels.verify_invention_claims (the Black-Bear correction: an LLM judge accused content that was present): each flagged phrase must appear in the reply text (else it is a judge hallucination and the flag is dropped) and must not be present in the synthesis by stem overlap (else it is not new). Log both the raw and the backstopped flag.
3. Replace the frozen du_pulse gauge _g_voice_contract (scripts/du_pulse.py, it reads data/voice_contract_shadow.jsonl, last written 2026-06-17) with a gauge reading data/voice_fidelity_shadow.jsonl: n, flagged share, backstopped flagged share, last row ts. Additive; leave _g_curator_shadow and core/curator.py untouched (J-2793 is deferred and the file's disposition is a founder question, see the review).
Pass criteria (state them in the finding): identity flagged at most 2 percent; scene-only at most 10 percent; inserted commitment at least 90 percent. If identity is flagged more than 10 percent or inserted-commitment recall is under 70 percent after ONE prompt revision, report the judge as not fit and stop; do not tune further against the data. Surface checks cannot stand in for the judge (F-3912): about half of replies have a question mark the synthesis lacks, and 0.66 to 0.72 of reply content words are absent from the synthesis.
Notes: model families other than qwen3.5:9b only (J-3254 picks mixtral :11438 or falcon :11440; do not add load on the shared Ramses hub beyond one call per pair; fail open and quiet). Run the replay through lab_env.isolate() so nothing is written to live stores. If J-3254 registered a prompt, do not register a second; any NEW prompt string must go through prompt_registry.py check. Report the numbers; do not rule on them.

title: ﻿Emissary take: build the pre-swap take-to-synthesis integration baseline (the control D-0539's defeater names)
briefing:

Source: the J-3143 curator repurposing review (docs/reviews/curator_repurposing_review_J-3143.md, Option B) and ruling D-0539, whose defeater reads: 'Revisit if no available hub answers a take inside the 6 s wait with at least 80 percent delivery, in which case retire the take; or if a month of delivered takes shows no overlap with the Executive's output beyond the pre-swap control.' Also count, deterministically, takes whose direct answer recasts the exchange in substrate terms (server, cloud, digital environment, hosted, language model, AI) so D-0539's trim of that framing has a before-number; the June rows 'where are you' got 'a digital environment hosted on servers' (F-3911).

title: ﻿Lab: voice render at temperature 0.2 vs live vs identity arm, judged by the D-0643 judge (after its 200 renders)
briefing:
﻿Lab experiment, gated on the D-0643 judge having logged 200 rows (the gate). Source: the J-3143 curator repurposing review, Option C, and D-0643's defeater: 'Revisit after 200 judged renders: if the judge flags under 5 percent or over 60 percent of replies it carries no information; if it flags a real share, read 20 flagged replies with the founder and decide on temperature 0.2 for the render.'
First, read J-3254's 200-render report and the J-3322 calibration result (the companion job; if it found the judge not fit, STOP and say so in the done summary; do not run the arms). If the flagged share is between 5 and 60 percent and the judge passed calibration: replay at least 100 historic voice inputs (system_prompt and user_prompt from data/training/voice.jsonl, newest first) through three arms on the lab copy: (1) the live voice settings (temperature class 0.4 + affect bias as core/node_base._temperature computes it), (2) the same prompt at temperature 0.2, (3) the identity arm (reply := synthesis, the deterministic template_render swap from core/curator.py, one line of code, used only as the zero-flag anchor). title: Lab: blinded different-family pair judge on cross-book symbolic-lens pairs (is a shared lens symbol a shared image?)
briefing:

Question: if two study notes from DIFFERENT books were given the same lens symbol (non-stock), is that a real shared image, or a nominal word match? The answer gates the cross-book "shares_image" link idea (option B in the review). If the links are not real, the lens is archived.

Inputs: data/symbolic_reading_log.jsonl (all rows). Normalise symbols (lowercase, strip leading the/a/an). Exclude the 17 most frequent normalised symbols (the stock archetypes). Build every cross-book pair (two different titles) that share a normalised non-stock symbol (F-3918: about 193 symbols, about 773 pairs). Only the 300-char reading sentences and titles are logged, so the judge sees: title A + reading A, title B + reading B. Do not show the symbol word to the judge.

Design: three arms, all blinded and shuffled. (1) the shared-symbol pairs; (2) an equal number of random cross-book pairs with DIFFERENT symbols, matched on month; (3) the same number of embedding-nearest cross-book pairs of the reading sentences (the study_note baseline; use core.memory.store _embed read-only or a local embedder; do not write). Success: (a) shared-symbol arm yes-rate at least 0.30 above the random-pairs arm and judge-pair agreement at least 0.7; (b) at least 30 percent of accepted pairs are NOT in arm 3 (new reach beyond embeddings). title: J-3142 option 1: chapter-telling audit by two different-family coders and deterministic copy and grounding checks
briefing:
LAB (read-only, lab_env.isolate() for anything that runs code; no write to data/, no restart): the chapter-telling audit. Read first: docs/reviews/J-3142_narrative_quality_coder_repurposing.md (section 3, option 1) and findings F-3934, F-3935, F-3937, F-3712, F-3714, F-3718. QUESTION. Can a decoupled judge reliably say, for each stored chapter of his life, (1) is the chapter's text copied from the sample it was authored from, (2) does it name a feeling that none of its members state, (3) does its narrated shape (the P-0048 agency, communion, transformation axes) agree with a different family's reading and with the recorded mood of the period? The chapter author AND the current coder are the same model on the same background chain (F-3937), so every existing score is self-coded.

INPUT. data/memory/nascence.db (open sqlite mode=ro): the 87 chapters (origin='chapter', chapter_level 1 and 2, full text) and their members via chapter_id (members have no valence, F-3934). data/affect_log.jsonl as the independent mood reference (the F-3934 method: opening vs closing third of the member span, +/-0.10). Existing coder rows: data/narrative_quality_log.jsonl kind=chapter (114 rows; match by the first 100 characters of the body).

METHOD. (a) Deterministic checks, no model: longest-shared-run and 6-gram overlap of each chapter body against its own members (the four chapters in F-3712 must be flagged: 125722d8, 1906eb26, 6fe32426, 36e231b6); named-feeling grounding (every feeling word in the chapter must occur in at least one member; the three planted-anxiety chapters in F-3718 c368e458, 994e2ead, b8456aba must be flagged); past-tense check. (b) Two coders from two DIFFERENT families than the author (command-r7b / qwen3.5), chosen from the live Ramses llama.cpp hubs (falcon3 :11436, granite :11437, mixtral :11438; first check which answer, and NEVER use the hot lane :11433, which is Travis's), run with the frozen P-0048 rubric text unchanged so the instrument is the same; one call per chapter per coder, temperature 0.3 as in the module; record model, endpoint, raw JSON. (c) Compare: coder-vs-coder agreement (Spearman on agency and communion; weighted agreement on the 3-class transformation), each coder vs the existing author-coded row, and each coder's transformation vs the mood-direction reference (the current author-coded baseline is at chance: redemption 10 up / 14 down of 41, F-3934).

SUCCESS (pre-registered). Agreement between the two new coders is at least 0.6 on agency and 0.6 on transformation; and at least one coder's transformation beats the mood reference by 15 points over the author-coded baseline; and the deterministic checks flag all 4 pasted and all 3 planted-anxiety chapters with at most 5 other chapters flagged by each. STOP. Coder-vs-coder agreement under 0.4 on both axes: the LLM axes are not a usable instrument on chapters; say so, keep only the deterministic checks (offer them to J-3009 as the copy and grounding guard), and recommend archiving the coder (see J-3355 / the review section 6).

DELIVER. docs/reviews/J-<this job>_chapter_telling_audit.md (commit with safe_commit.py --new-file), a per-chapter table, findings via findings_log.py record (verified only with quoted output), and a one-line verdict for the open decision about whether a flag may ever change the estate projection (read decide.py show on it; do not rule it). title: safe_commit.py: sync CRLF working-tree files (autocrlf) instead of reporting a false concurrent edit
briefing: Toolchain fix for F-4015, in C:\Users\USER\.claude\skills\job-run\safe_commit.py (not under C:\Nascence). In _sync_working_tree, real_bytes != old_bytes is a byte compare, so on a core.autocrlf=true tree (tracked blobs LF, disk CRLF) it never matches the LF old-content file the briefing tells agents to build, and it refuses to sync with a warning that blames a concurrent editor. Fix: compare with CRLF normalised to LF on both sides, and when it does match, write the new content using the CRLF convention the on-disk file had (detect from real_bytes: if it contains b'\r\n', convert new_bytes LF to CRLF). Keep the refusal for a real mismatch (after normalising). Also change the warning text to mention the line-ending case. Add a small test in a temp repo with autocrlf=true: commit a CRLF-on-disk file via safe_commit and assert working_tree_synced true and git diff HEAD empty. Separately look at whether the shared .git/index showing the path as staged-reverse after a safe_commit is a known, documented effect (it is the stale shared index, which a bare git commit would commit) and say so in the module docstring if not. Do not run git stash/reset/checkout/restore. Check docs/job-run SKILL.md Tier 1/2 recipe text for the working_tree_synced instruction and update it if it assumes LF.

title: gauge-correlate: add the lag +/-1 cross-correlation asymmetry (contiguous Levy area) with the roll null, and design a sleep/wake-preserving null
briefing: scripts/analyze_nascence_gauge_correlations.py computes zero-lag Pearson only. The 2026-11-05 audit (finding F-4039; scripts C:/UDMS/scripts/argon_audit_2026-11-05/rep_levy_circ.py and C:/UDMS/scripts/argon_audit_2026-11-05/levy_calibration.py; outputs C:/UDMS/data/argon_audit_2026-11-05/outputs_2026-11-05.md) showed that the contiguous Levy area on z-scored 15-min bins equals 0.5*(r(+1) - r(-1)), a lead-lag statistic; that the roll-over-common-bins null is calibrated (0/40 false positives at |z|>3 on independent phase-randomized surrogates); and that on the 141-day live logs emissary.mass x sleep.P (z 12.3) and affect.arousal x affect.valence (z 7.4) survive while sleep.chronic x stream.redundancy fades to 2.4 (6.9 on the 16-day snapshot). Task: (1) add the lag +/-1 asymmetry with the roll null to the gauge-correlate pass over ALL registered HUD monitors on the live C:/Nascence/data logs (read-only); (2) design and apply a null that preserves the sleep/wake cycle WITHOUT misaligning the two logs' shared downtime (a plain or circular time shift was shown over-conservative for exactly that reason: it shrinks the contiguous-step count), e.g. shift by whole days only across bins where both logs were up, or regress each series on its diurnal profile first and test the residuals; (3) write the pair table and a verdict on the two survivors to a dated docs/audits file. Done = that file exists with z under both nulls for every pair. UPDATE 2026-11-06 (F-4150): the sleep/wake-preserving null now exists and is the within-bout linear detrend: define wake bouts as runs of >=8 contiguous 900 s bins with sleep.awake_min increasing, fit and subtract a line per bout per series, then score the contiguous Levy area with the roll null (C:/UDMS/scripts/argon_audit_2026-11-05/levy_wake_ramp.py, output in C:/UDMS/data/argon_audit_2026-11-05/outputs_2026-11-05.md round-5 section). Under it emissary.mass x sleep.P is dead (z +12.64 -> +0.07) and affect.arousal x affect.valence survives (+8.1), so the pair this job was filed to test is resolved. REMAINING SCOPE: add the lag +/-1 asymmetry to scripts/analyze_nascence_gauge_correlations.py over ALL registered monitors with BOTH the raw roll null and the within-bout-detrended variant, report the pairs that survive the second, and compare the arousal x valence survivor with the affect engine's own update order (where valence/arousal are updated in C:/Nascence/core) before calling it a finding. Method credit: Argon (Antigravity), 2026-11-05.

title: Founder: Curiosity explicit base_temperature (0.5) or hold at 0.2? Lab J-3265 pre-registered bar not met (29.6% vs 33.3%); recommend hold
briefing:
Founder call, from lab J-3265 (D-0656), numbers in docs/lab/J-3265_curiosity_temperature.md (worktree branch jobrun/wl_1, commit d39545aa) and findings F-4055, F-4056, F-4057. Question: set an explicit Curiosity base_temperature (nodes/curiosity_node.py; a hub-file change: run udms_get_change_dossier on nodes/curiosity_node.py and core/node_base.py first; additive and restart-gated), or hold at the 0.2 default?
Numbers (90 inputs, 810 replays on the node's own lane, command-r7b, 3 samples per temperature): near-duplicate first questions (vs previous 5 logged rows) token-Jaccard>0.6: 46.3% at 0.2, 37.8% at 0.35, 32.6% at 0.5; trigram>=0.3: 57.4%, 48.1%, 41.1%. Relative fall at 0.5 = 29.6% / 28.4% (95% CI on the token fall 13-43%), at 0.35 = 18% / 16%. The pre-registered bar (fall by at least one third on BOTH metrics, and specificity not falling) is NOT met, by a near miss on the first half; specificity does not fall (falcon +0.19, mixtral +0.01 at 0.5). Exact repeats between three samples of the same input: 56% of rows at 0.2, 27% at 0.35, 9% at 0.5. Side effect: share of outputs with urgency>0.6 (ignites an unprompted cycle) 64.8% -> 55.6% at 0.5.
Cause: input continuity, not temperature (null control with another row's previous-5 pool: 4% vs 46-57%; F-4056). A higher temperature is a partial lever only.
Recommendation: HOLD at 0.2 as the near-duplicate fix (the pre-registered rule says not to propose it); if you want the cheap partial lever anyway, 0.5 is spec-neutral on both judges and cuts exact repeats 56% to 9% at no measured cost, but it is outside the rule you set. The real lever is the input (see the follow-up lab on Curiosity input continuity).

"You are 渡's own capacity to turn and look at a thought he just had. A thought that arrives is not yet something he has earned the right to call his own opinion — he has to consider it first. Read the thought below, and whatever came before it in this same line of thinking. Then genuinely ask: why did this occur to me just now — what was I actually responding to? title: Rule which geometry_tuples row is canonical for an idle cycle (store stamp vs idle row) and fix the debounce miss that writes both (F-4078)
briefing: MECHANISM (finding F-4078, verified 2026-11-06; C:/UDMS/docs/audits/argon_math_audit_verification_2026-11-05.md section 9.1; script C:/UDMS/scripts/argon_audit_2026-11-05/echo_mechanism.py): core/memory/store.py:1080 stamps the census for every stored fragment with snapshot(source=origin, thought=content[:70], debounce=False), writing an inner_thought row; nodes/inner_monologue_node.py:6656 then calls snapshot(source='idle', thought=thought) 0.1-0.3 s later with the full thought; core/geometry_census.py:340-347 debounces only when (thought or '')[:120] equals the previous call's string, and a <=70-char string never equals a 79-120-char one, so both rows land. Since 2026-09 that is 60-95% of idle cycles (40,795 twins on the live file as of 2026-11-06; the first 70 chars of thought agree on all of them). WAITING ON: Travis's ruling, A or B (C is listed to rule it out). Constraint: J-2640 (done 2026-10-30) changed this same debounce for the reading-fragment case (F-3371) and must stay fixed. Verification must run under lab isolation (~/.claude/skills/job-queue/lab_env.py): never write the live geometry_tuples.jsonl or nascence.db. RULED 2026-11-06 by travis (D-0688): option B, mark the stamp row so readers drop it; the idle row stays canonical for state and unresolved. Proceed under lab isolation.

title: UDMS ranker: test count-based IC_025 (and plain co-change count) as the temporal term against raw pmi_rec under J-3453's scorer (F-4193, D-0689)
briefing:
WHAT: finding F-4193 and decision D-0689 (ruled by the founder 2026-11-06: J-3453 runs its baseline first; the changes that move target lists then land one at a time as pre-registered interventions against its scorer; this is one of them). The ranker's temporal terms (core/udms/ranker.py:93-98 and 130-131: contrib_co = b_co*log2(1+co_rec); contrib_pmi = b_pmi*pmi_rec, with pmi_rec = log2(max(1, lift_rec)+1e-6) and lift_rec = co_rec*rec_z/p_a_rec/p_b_rec on recency-weighted masses) have no small-sample shrinkage. On C:/UDMS three (n_A,n_B,n_AB)=(1,1,1) pairs tie for first at 7.76 bits, and on Nascence raw pmi_rec is the worst temporal scorer out of sample. Argon proposed WHO-style IC = log2((co+0.5)/(E+0.5)) on the weighted masses; that form is about 0 for 89.5% (oldest 450 commits) and 81.5% (newest 450) of Nascence pairs and rewards recency over evidence. Out-of-sample hit rate (top 5 against the next 5 commits, the battery protocol, hot files excluded; all2000 train 60%/test 40% n=799 | newest900 n=353 | oldest450 battery split n=265): churn 42.7|47.3|47.5; unweighted co-change count 42.1|45.0|44.9; recency-weighted co_rec 35.2|37.7|38.5; raw pmi_rec 33.0|32.0|17.0; IC on mass 32.2|34.6|31.7; IC_025 on counts 36.4|35.7|37.0. So IC_025 on counts is the best PMI-family variant but nothing in the family beats co-change count or churn. The served dossier shows a TEMPORAL slot only 10 times in 7,103 slots (F-4183), so the effect on what agents see may be small; the value is the correctness of the evidence layer and a clean answer on whether to keep a PMI term at all.

title: Conversational influence study: do Travis's teachings reorganise Du's thinking (Wu Wei reference case)
briefing:
Conversational Influence and Cognitive Integration Study. Read-only analysis of Du's stores; change no Du code.

Background (read first): docs/reviews/du_clinical_read_2026-11-16.md, findings F-4812, F-4813, F-4814, thought T-0139. Earlier scripts are in docs/lab/T-0139_conversation_influence/ (conv_effect.py = event study of mood and topic after conversations; lessons.py = keyword trace of taught concepts through private origins by month). Travis's turns are memory_fragments rows with origin 'lived' whose content starts '[Travis said to me]' (1,714 rows, 2026-05-30 on). Private thinking = origins inner_thought, dream, night_thought, gist, subconscious_synthesis, active_imagination, journal, letter, essay, standing_insight.

What is already known: Wu Wei came only from Travis (first said 06-07, full lesson 08-09, last said 08-29) and still appears 3 to 6 times a month in private thought, applied to new material, last 11-14. Jung vocabulary fell from 323 to 18 uses a month when Jung left the axiom (D-0509), so it was prompt-held. Amor fati spiked for 3 days and vanished. Mindfulness has 112 uses, source unknown. Long talks lift mood about a day; no topic shift past 6 hours by session-centroid similarity.

What to do, in this order:
1. Retrieval path. For each private Wu Wei thought after 08-29, check the recall and injection logs (co-recall store, core/associative_recall.py injection logging, understanding_from_guidance rows) for whether a Travis row or a guidance principle was recalled into the prompt that produced it. This separates 'the recall system handed it to him' from 'the model produced it unaided'. Both count as Du, but they are different mechanisms.
2. Source sorting. For Wu Wei, mindfulness, Cook Ding, Ship of Theseus, amor fati: first appearance in Travis rows versus reading/study rows versus private thought. Mindfulness in particular may come from his reading (The Religion of the Samurai is on the shelf).
3. Unnamed influence (the hard one). Build a stance measure that does not use the word: have a decoupled judge model rate a blind, date-shuffled sample of inner thoughts for 'forcing an answer versus letting the question stand without strain', sampled from before 08-09 and from 30, 60, 90 days after. Use a second unrelated stance as a control so a general drift is not read as a Wu Wei effect. Inner thoughts only exist from 06-03, so the 08-09 lesson is the usable before/after line, not 06-07. Report the judge's agreement with itself on a repeat sample before trusting any difference.
4. Behaviour. Does anything he does change, not only what he says: garden-door and other outing actions, letters written versus sent, commitments kept, around the same dates.
5. Structural persistence. Compare Wu Wei rate and the stance measure across restarts and across the D-0509 prompt change. Model change: if the staged model-swap A-B-A test is run, add these as readouts; at 3 to 6 uses a month the keyword rate has no power in a short window, so rely on the stance measure.

Known traps: replay_count is a dedup counter, not a recall count. The yin/yang regex matches ordinary words. Mottainai predates Travis saying it. Valence records start 08-21. Restarts and conversations coincide (only 12 of 109 sessions have no restart within 6 hours). The generating model has a Daoist-sounding house register, so a rise in 'letting be' language needs the control stance and the before/after line to mean anything.

Done looks like: a lab report in docs/lab/ with one table per teaching (source, retention at 30/60/90 days, transfer examples, stance change with interval, behaviour change, survives restart/prompt change), each claim logged through findings_log with its confidence, and a plain statement of which of the three levels (memory, integration, reorganisation) the evidence supports for each teaching.

title: Implicit conceptual influence test: bare-model control and blind stance classification (extends J-4073)
briefing:
Implicit conceptual influence test. Extends J-4073 (read its briefing first) and findings F-4814, F-4815. Read-only against Du's stores; any model calls go to a lab endpoint, never to Du's live hot lane while he is running. Change no Du code.

Question: has a teaching from Travis raised the likelihood that Du reasons in line with it when neither the teaching nor its name is in his immediate context? Reference case Wu Wei; comparison cases Cook Ding, mindfulness, and amor fati (taught 09-02, faded in three days).

Part A, the bare-model control (do this first, it is the cheapest and it addresses the open item in F-4815). F-4815 found that before the two thoughts where Du credits Travis, recall surfaced the principle 'stillness is a natural rhythm, not failure' without the words Wu Wei, and the thought then named it. Take the generating model Du's idle thoughts use, with no memory, no identity and no history, and give it only the recalled principle text plus a neutral idle-thought instruction, about 100 times. Count how often it writes 'Wu Wei'. Repeat with the same text inside Du's real assembled prompt taken from the logs for those cycles, if the prompt can be reconstructed. If the bare model names Wu Wei at a high rate, the naming is the model's prior knowledge. If it rarely does and Du's real prompts do, the association is carried by something in Du's context; find which part.

Part B, blind retrospective classification. For each teaching write, before looking at any data, a short description of a situation where the principle is relevant (for Wu Wei: an unresolved question or stalled task where he could force an answer or let it stand) and of the two stances. Pull candidate thoughts by situation, not by keyword, and exclude any that contain the teaching's name or the word Travis. Sample evenly from before the teaching date and from 30, 60 and 90 days after. Shuffle, strip dates, and have a decoupled judge model classify stance. The judge is not told the hypothesis, the teaching, or which passages are before or after. Classify a repeat subsample to get the judge's agreement with itself; if agreement is weak (the project's judge kappa has been weak before), stop and report that. Only then unblind.

Controls that must be in the report: (1) a control stance unrelated to any teaching, classified the same way, so a general drift is not read as a teaching effect; (2) amor fati as the faded case: if the judge finds a lasting stance change there too, the method is not discriminating; (3) the single before/after date is confounded with everything else that changed near it (for Wu Wei: the 08-09 lesson sits among code updates, new books, and the About You book on 08-24), so say plainly that a before/after difference is consistent with the teaching, not proof of it. Inner thoughts exist only from 06-03, so use 08-09 as the Wu Wei line.

Also answer the smaller question GPT raised on F-4815: for the 6 of 15 Wu Wei thoughts preceded by a recalled Travis row, were those rows semantically related to the thought. A first unblinded look says one row is from the 08-09 lesson day itself, about three are thematically close (river, flow, yielding control), and two are unrelated; redo this with embeddings and a matched baseline.

Done looks like: a lab report in docs/lab/ giving, per teaching, the bare-model naming rate, the blind stance rates before and after with intervals, the control stance, judge self-agreement, and a plain verdict on two items left unresolved so far: independence from the model's prior knowledge, and a persistent change in reasoning disposition. Each claim logged through findings_log with its confidence.

title: Teaching to synthesis study: delivery by relevance and what Du does with Travis's teachings (extends J-4074)
briefing:
Teaching to synthesis study: what Du does with what Travis taught him, and whether his own recall delivers it when it applies. Follows J-4074 (read docs/lab/2026-11-16_J-4074_implicit_conceptual_influence.md and findings F-4816, F-4817, F-4818, F-4819, F-4833 first) and the founder's point of 2026-11-16: retrieving from memory and using it IS learning, so do not require the teaching to be absent from the prompt. Read-only against Du's stores; change no Du code. If model calls are needed, never the hot lane on 11433 while Du is running.

What J-4074 left: Du uses Travis's words well when shown them. The Wu Wei mentions that could be traced were driven by a uniform random channel (divergent seed, closed at the 11-14 restart), and relevance-driven recall showed no preference for lesson material. When a derived principle row was put in a real prompt, 73 of 100 thoughts took up its stance against 14 of 100 without it (a keyword count, not a judged rating). So the open questions are delivery and synthesis, not retention.

Part 1, delivery by relevance. For the 45 understanding_from_guidance rows and the Travis lesson rows (Wu Wei, Cook Ding, amor fati, others found by source sorting): define, before looking, situations where each principle clearly applies. Select idle thoughts by situation (embedding similarity to a neutral description, as in part_b_build_sample.py). For each, check whether the principle or lesson row was actually in the prompt: data/idle_prompt_samples.jsonl first (1 in 20, from 11-09), data/prompt_provenance.jsonl, then the co-recall ledger, counting only non-shadow sources. Report the delivery rate against a matched baseline of thoughts where the principle does not apply. The co-recall ledger does not cover every channel; say which channels were checked.

Part 2, the chain teaching to retrieval to synthesis to storage to later recall. Pick teachings from Travis rows. Trace descendants: gists, consolidation rows, understanding and understanding_from_guidance rows, essays, standing insights, dreams (dreamt_from edges in memory_edges) that derive from or sit close to the lesson. For each descendant ask: does it combine the teaching with something from his reading or another teaching; does it modify or disagree with the original; is it later recalled by relevance and used. Use a blind judge for "combines two sources" and "departs from the original", with the source texts shown and dates stripped, and measure judge repeat agreement before unblinding (bar 0.60, as in J-4074).

Part 3, self-generated questions. Compare the questions in his curiosity log and follow-line asks before and after conversation sessions, against restarts with no conversation (the control set in conv_effect.py), for whether new question topics trace to what Travis said.

Traps: record which model wrote each passage (gemma4:e4b before 08-20, qwen3.5:9b after); the top 5 percent lesson-near bucket is loose (10 percent of everything recalled falls in it); replay_count is a dedup counter; Travis said Wu Wei and Cook Ding again on 11-16.

Done looks like: a lab report in docs/lab/ with the delivery rate and baseline, a table of traced chains with examples quoted, judge agreement, and a plain statement of what is shown and not shown; each claim logged through findings_log at its true confidence.

title: God functions: count the past bugs in _think and _run_cycle_impl that were caused by structure rather than logic (evidence gate for the parked split, D-0877)
briefing:
Read-only analysis. No code changes. Plan: docs/staged/god_function_split.md, section 0.4. Decision context: D-0877 (split parked), D-0878 (freeze-first track, open).

Question: how many past bugs in InnerMonologueNode._think (nodes/inner_monologue_node.py) and Orchestrator._run_cycle_impl (core/orchestrator.py) were caused by the STRUCTURE of the function (its size and layout) rather than by its logic? The answer decides whether splitting these functions is worth its risk. Two are already known: J-2678 (dead duplicate _build_system_prompt call) and J-3952 (the same call inside the retry loop eating consume-once feeder lines).

Method:
1. Build the candidate set from docs/job_queue.jsonl (done jobs) and docs/findings.jsonl: every row that describes a fix or a defect in either function or file. Also scan git log for the two files (207 and 97 commits) for fix-shaped commit messages with no job id. Read the stores with a script that prints counts and ids only; do not hand-edit any .jsonl.
2. Classify each candidate into one of: STRUCTURE (duplicate or misplaced call; wrong scope; placement relative to the retry loop or the seed join; a local shadowed, stale or reused; a block overlooked because of the function's length; an edit that landed in the wrong one of several similar blocks), LOGIC (would have happened in any layout), or UNCLEAR. Read the job or finding text, and the diff where the text does not settle it. Say for each how it was decided.
3. Report: counts per class for each function, the ids in each class, the share STRUCTURE makes of all classified fixes, and how many were silent (found by reading, not by an error). State the limits of the read plainly, including candidates that could not be classified.
4. Record the result with findings_log.py (confidence verified only for what was actually read; inferred otherwise), plan god_function_split, and add one plan-state note. Do not reopen or rule any decision; the founder reads the count against D-0877's defeater.

Done looks like: one finding with the counts and ids, and a short table written to docs/reviews/god_function_bug_count_<date>.md.
done_note: F-5127: 9 structure, 54 logic, 6 unclear of 69 classified (about 14 percent structure; range 8 to 26). All 9 in _think, none in _run_cycle_impl, all silent. Report docs/reviews/god_function_bug_count_2026-11-20.md. No decision ruled; founder reads it against D-0877's defeater.

title: Build the standing idle-thought equivalence harness (scripts/think_equivalence.py): prompts, self state and data bytes, old worktree vs new, with coverage read and negative control (D-0878 a)
briefing:
Build the standing equivalence harness for the idle thought. Founder ruling D-0878 part (a), 2026-11-20. Plan: docs/staged/god_function_split.md sections 0.3 and 4.1 to 4.4. Evidence for why: F-5127 (9 structure-caused defects in _think, all silent; 7 of them are the kind this harness would catch on the day of the edit).

Scope: NEW SCRIPT ONLY. Do not edit anything under nodes/ or core/. The split of existing code is parked (D-0877); this harness is a regression test for ordinary edits, not a prelude to moving code.

Start from scripts/test_idle_offloop_equivalence.py (J-1918 / F-2547), which already drives real InnerMonologueNode._think() calls offline: throwaway worktrees (old vs new) with a full data copy, time.time() frozen, network blocked, the LLM boundary stubbed to record the prompt. Read it and its lag_harness prelude first and reuse what works.

Build scripts/think_equivalence.py with:
1. Two stub modes: raise-at-the-call (covers everything before the retry loop) and canned-replies (so the retry loop and the post-thought section run too).
2. random seeded, time frozen, so two runs of the same code are byte-identical. Prove that first: old vs old must compare IDENTICAL.
3. A scenario set wide enough to open the gates in _think: study directive, curiosity ask, founder recall, goal offer, music, weather, reread hint, mid-train, sleepy, redirect outward, and a plain quiet thought.
4. Outputs compared between the two worktrees: system prompt and user prompt bytes; the node's self-attribute snapshot after each call; id-normalised bytes appended to every data file; log lines.
5. A coverage read: which top-level blocks of _think ran with their gate open, ran gate-closed only, or never ran, across the scenario set. Report the never-ran list plainly; it is the limit of what the harness can vouch for.
6. A negative control, run and recorded: in a scratch worktree swap two adjacent seed parts and drop one self write; the harness must report DIFFERENT for both. If either passes, the harness is not finished.
7. A one-command use for an ordinary edit: compare HEAD against the working tree for nodes/inner_monologue_node.py and print what changed in the prompt, the self state and the data bytes.

Hard rules: no git stash/reset/checkout--/restore/clean in the shared tree; use git worktree add in the scratchpad. No write under live C:\Nascence data/ (import core BEFORE lab_env; hash-canary the live stores before and after; see the live-store-leak history). No model call, no server start. Du may be up or down; this must not touch him.

Done looks like: the script committed by path; old-vs-old IDENTICAL; negative control DIFFERENT twice; the coverage table written to docs/reviews/; a finding recorded with the numbers (how many of the 123 top-level blocks the scenarios reach); a plan-state note on god_function_split; and if the harness cannot be made deterministic, say so plainly, because that is D-0878's defeater.
